articles.title: Notifications, social media and more with BBC Sport
articles.summary: With latest scores and headlines sent straight to your device, personalisation and much more, ensure you have a great sporting life with BBC Sport.
articles.body:
Want all the biggest sports news, analysis and scores sent direct to your phone or tablet? Then download the BBC Sport app.

The app also comes with all our website content along with a radio player, Chromecast integration, a widget and personalised menu options. It's free and easy to download - simply head to the relevant link below:

Download the BBC Sport app: Apple , external - Android , external - Amazon , external

The BBC Sport app offers two types of notification.

With news notifications you can have the biggest sport stories and the best content right at your fingertips. Stay in the know by picking from our offering of top sport headlines, football news - including the biggest updates, features and analysis on your Premier League, Championship and Scottish Premiership club - and news from nine other major sports, as well as the best from each nation of the United Kingdom. You can also sign up to get alerts to our latest Insight in-depth features.

You can also follow your team from wherever you are with our massive range of event notifications. We offer notifications across five sports - football, cricket, Formula 1, rugby union and rugby league - covering every major moment. Line-ups, kick-offs, and half-time scores, goals, wickets, tries and conversions, results and times on the wave of the chequered flag. We serve more than 400 teams, with more to come.

Follow the biggest moments from matches and events in real time, straight from your lock screen - without needing to open the BBC Sport app.

When you follow a team in the app, Live Activities and Live Updates can keep you up to date as the action happens, including goals, key moments and major match developments.

Live Activities are available on iOS 16 and above.

Live Updates are available on Android 16 QPR2 and above.

To receive them, you'll need to have Live Activities enabled on iOS, or Live Updates and notifications enabled on Android.

You might want to add Commonwealth Games, cricket, tennis, boxing and squash - by doing so your My Sport area will display the latest articles and videos from those topics, and also relevant information such as latest scores and results.

articles.title: A last-second goal ends the World Cup honeymoon for Mauricio Pochettino and the USA. Now the real work begins
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino said he was happy. He said it in English, he said it in his native Spanish. He swore he was happy.
articles.body: Mauricio Pochettino said he was happy. He said it in English, he said it in his native Spanish. He swore he was happy. He didn’t sound happy. And really, there wasn’t much of a reason to be. A little more than an hour before his post-match press conference in the bowels of SoFi Stadium, Pochettino watched his USA team give up a last-second goal to Turkey that ensured a 3-2 defeat in this final match of the group stage. A weakened US side – nine changes were made from the team that faced Australia last week in Seattle – had scored quickly, gave up two first-half goals and then equalized in a strong second half. But a goal from Kaan Ayhan, scored with the last kick of the game, handed the US its first defeat after two dominant victories to open the tournament. And with it, he may have ended the honeymoon for this USA team. Pochettino’s surly mood after the game – brushing off questions about momentum, chastising American journalists for not congratulating him for winning Group D – was a marked change from the gregarious figure who sat in the same chair a little more than 24 hours before. The question now is if that mood was indicative of the vibes around this US team changing ahead of the knockout stages now that the bubble of invincibility has been popped. “I think it’s all positive, and I am so positive, and I am happy,” Pochettino said in answer to a question about whether the US may have lost momentum. “Maybe I am not showing (it) because your questions are a little bit weird, but I am so happy, and the players are happy because I think we perform, we compete, and we are first. “I was talking with the Turkish channel now, as I said, ‘Have a good trip back to Turkey,’ and we are going on. But I think now when I arrive here (in the press conference) – maybe I am confused – but maybe the mood is like we go home tonight and Turkey stay.” Pochettino is, of course, right on some very important points. By winning its first two games of this World Cup, the USA locked up the top spot in Group D and has a Round of 32 matchup against Bosnia and Herzegovina set for July 1 in the San Francisco Bay Area. It’s exactly what this team would have hoped for when the tournament started and gives them a favorable path for a deep tournament run. His lineup on Thursday, which consisted of eight players making their first World Cup starts, showed off the depth of his team as key players like Tyler Adams, Folarin Balogun, Chris Richards and Antonee Robinson were able to rest and avoid possible suspension for the game against the Zmajevi. Despite the multitude of changes, the Americans started the game well with an opening goal in the third minute and then fought back to tie the match in the second half after Turkey finally got on the score sheet. And Christian Pulisic returned to action and looked like his game-changing best, coming on in the 58th minute and quickly providing scores of chances as the US took the game to the Turks. A loss is ultimately a harsh result on the Americans after the way they recovered in the second half, looking like the more likely side to score until the game reached the final minutes. “We are much better (now) than before that game because we are players now with 90 minutes in the legs and performing, and I think ready to help if we need from the beginning or after from the bench,” Pochettino said. Still, Pochettino’s tone indicated he was still annoyed to have lost. The way the loss came about should be raising alarm bells inside the US camp. Before the tournament began, it was no secret that the USA’s defending was suspect. While the Stars and Stripes can go forward at opposing goals with flair and intent, the backline has been known to give up goals. The shutout against Australia was the first time they’d kept a clean sheet since a friendly against Japan nearly a year before. With the games now having the kind of stakes that Thursday’s contest lacked, that leaky defense – especially in crunch time toward the end of matches – is the possible Achilles heel for this team. The Turks put the US under pressure for much of the first half and again in those final minutes, playing with the desperation of a team that didn’t want to leave this World Cup without getting at least one result. When the Bosnians take the pitch in Santa Clara in a little less than a week, they’ll likely bring that same verve as they play in their nation’s first World Cup knockout game. At times on Thursday, the US struggled to cope with that pressure. The Americans are used to being the team that brings the game to their opponent, not being the squad that is absorbing and repelling attacks. But when faced with their first real setback of this tournament, the US responded positively. The introduction of Pulisic in the second half will also be a reassuring takeaway from this contest as the AC Milan man looked likely to score from the moment he entered the fray and was the best part of what the US did after Sebastian Berhalter’s strike drew the Americans level. “I think it was important to for him to get the feelings I seen again after not to be able to available for Australia,” Pochettino said. “One of the objectives in that game, not only was to win, (it was) to provide Christian in between 30 and 40 minutes to get the feeling to be ready for the next game, that is important too.” The loss to Turkey doesn’t mean all that much in what the US has to do going forward. The squad knew who its next opponent would be, when it would be playing and where it was going next. Any worries about complacency were wiped away in the third minute when Auston Trusty fired home the opening goal and caused the stands at SoFi Stadium to shake (literally) with the noise and jumping fans. Sure, it was a starting lineup of players who are usually backups or impact subs. Sure, the result has no effect on the Americans’ path toward a deep run in the tournament. Sure, a lot of the mistakes or poor moments in defense can be waved away by recognizing that most of the team’s best defenders were sitting on the bench when the Turks wheeled away in delight with Ayhan’s goal. But results do not happen in a vacuum. American soccer fans had been stunned at the way this US team looked in its opening two games, finding themselves believing that a nation that has won one knockout game in the World Cup in its history could have the squad to make a run far into July. It felt like a new day was dawning in US men’s soccer. paragraphs: Mauricio Pochettino said he was happy. He said it in English, he said it in his native Spanish. He swore he was happy. He didn’t sound happy. And really, there wasn’t much of a reason to be. A little more than an hour before his post-match press conference in the bowels of SoFi Stadium, Pochettino watched his USA team give up a last-second goal to Turkey that ensured a 3-2 defeat in this final match of the group stage. A weakened US side – nine changes were made from the team that faced Australia last week in Seattle – had scored quickly, gave up two first-half goals and then equalized in a strong second half. But a goal from Kaan Ayhan, scored with the last kick of the game, handed the US its first defeat after two dominant victories to open the tournament. And with it, he may have ended the honeymoon for this USA team. Pochettino’s surly mood after the game – brushing off questions about momentum, chastising American journalists for not congratulating him for winning Group D – was a marked change from the gregarious figure who sat in the same chair a little more than 24 hours before. The question now is if that mood was indicative of the vibes around this US team changing ahead of the knockout stages now that the bubble of invincibility has been popped. “I think it’s all positive, and I am so positive, and I am happy,” Pochettino said in answer to a question about whether the US may have lost momentum. “Maybe I am not showing (it) because your questions are a little bit weird, but I am so happy, and the players are happy because I think we perform, we compete, and we are first. “I was talking with the Turkish channel now, as I said, ‘Have a good trip back to Turkey,’ and we are going on. Despite the multitude of changes, the Americans started the game well with an opening goal in the third minute and then fought back to tie the match in the second half after Turkey finally got on the score sheet. A loss is ultimately a harsh result on the Americans after the way they recovered in the second half, looking like the more likely side to score until the game reached the final minutes. “We are much better (now) than before that game because we are players now with 90 minutes in the legs and performing, and I think ready to help if we need from the beginning or after from the bench,” Pochettino said. At times on Thursday, the US struggled to cope with that pressure. The Americans are used to being the team that brings the game to their opponent, not being the squad that is absorbing and repelling attacks. Sure, it was a starting lineup of players who are usually backups or impact subs. Sure, the result has no effect on the Americans’ path toward a deep run in the tournament. Sure, a lot of the mistakes or poor moments in defense can be waved away by recognizing that most of the team’s best defenders were sitting on the bench when the Turks wheeled away in delight with Ayhan’s goal. It felt like a new day was dawning in US men’s soccer. The time to prove it comes in five days at Levi’s Stadium.

articles.title: Super League's Final Charge: Leeds Rhinos, Wakefield Trinity, Wigan Warriors, Warrington Wolves, Hull KR, Leigh Leopards and St Helens in contention
articles.summary: A look at the 'Final Charge' and how the last three rounds of the Super League season are shaping up; round 25 of Super League commences from Thursday August 27, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
There are just three rounds of Super League action remaining and, with it, a whole lot of drama as Super League's Final Charge ramps up.

In Super League, the two teams who finish first and second are guaranteed a home semi-final across Friday September 25 and Saturday September 26.

In the week prior to that, the Play-Off Eliminators occur in which the third-place team takes on the team in sixth and fourth plays fifth for the chance to make it into the semis.

  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want
  • Listen to The Bench, Sky's rugby league podcast

Then the winners of the semi-finals head to the Grand Final at Old Trafford on Saturday October 3.

Let's take a look at what each team has remaining and what is on the line for them...

1) Leeds Rhinos (38 points)

Leeds Rhinos have been at the summit of Super League for a while now and they will want to hold onto that for their three remaining fixtures.

However, they are now level on points with Wigan, who briefly leapfrogged them with Friday's win over Wakefield, but they have a vastly-superior points difference after Sunday's rout of York.

They last won the League Leaders' Shield way back in 2015 and last won a trophy in 2020 when they took Challenge Cup glory, so finishing top would see a welcome return of some silverware for the Rhinos.

In their last three matches, they face St Helens (A), Wigan Warriors (A) and Hull FC (H).

After the tricky trip to face Saints, they crucially host the Warriors on September 5 so their run-in is far from an easy on, but if they can now remain unbeaten, League Leaders' Shield glory will be theirs and they will be one match from walking out at the 'Theatre of Dreams' once again.

2) Wigan Warriors (38 points)

The team who have been there, done that, and got the T-shirt. Matt Peet, head coach of Wigan, has made no secret of how hard he has been pushing for a top-two finish because he knows how crucial that home semi-final is.

Now, if his team continue on, they could usurp Leeds if they keep the pressure on with their play-off spot confirmed.

Not only that, the Warriors will be hungry to avenge their Grand Final defeat to Hull KR in 2025.

They have the Challenge Cup in their trophy cabinet and will have all eyes on adding a second piece of silverware.

Ahead of the play-offs, they still have to play Hull KR (H), Leeds Rhinos (A) and Catalans Dragons (H).

3) Warrington Wolves (36 points)

Warrington Wolves made it three wins in a jam-packed 10 days by beating Huddersfield Giants to move on to 36 points.

Their 34-24 triumph against Huddersfield on Sunday was a fifth consecutive win, putting them in the right form at the right time for the play-off charge with just three rounds to go, and they could yet even snatch top spot.

In their remaining fixtures, they face Hull FC (A), Wakefield Trinity (A) and Toulouse Olympique (H).

All of those teams are below them in the table - a luxury not afforded to many other teams in the play-off picture.

The game against Wakefield will be the toughest test, with Trinity just four points below them.

4) Wakefield Trinity (32 points)

What a season it has been for Wakefield Trinity.

They are on the hunt for their highest Super League finish, but will now want to bounce back following their heart-breaking two-point defeat to top-of-the-table Leeds and then subsequent defeats to St Helens and Wigan Warriors.

In honesty, with two top teams remaining in their run-in, those results should worry Daryl Powell's side.

They have games against York Knights (H), Warrington Wolves (H) and Leigh Leopards (A) left.

Those are against two teams out of the seven still in the fight.

5) Leigh Leopards (32 points)

The team that has become renowned for coming good when they need to, Leigh Leopards want to shore up their spot in the play-offs once again.

After a disastrous start to the season, Adrian Lam's side have found their groove, made waves and look in real good nick at present.

Indeed, their win over Leeds set down a marker.

However, they have a tough end to the season in which they will know every win will matter.

The Leopards face Huddersfield Giants (A), St Helens (H) and Wakefield Trinity (H).

If Leigh want to make it to the Grand Final for the first time, they need to continue to show their steel now.

6) Hull KR (30 points)

Hull KR are right in the mix and will want it to stay that way but after their loss to Warrington, they are two points off fourth spot with three games left.

The Robins were the team who did it all in 2025, ending the wait for a new team to win the competition, and now they will want to send coach Willie Peters out on a high by going back to back.

Their shock loss to Toulouse did not help their cause, though.

Their remaining matches are against Wigan Warriors (A), Huddersfield Giants (H) and St Helens (A).

7) St Helens (28 points)

St Helens have three matches to try and ensure they do not make some unwanted history.

Saints have never missed out on the play-offs. Most recently they lost 20-12 to Hull KR in the semi-finals in 2025 as the Robins went on to complete the treble.

After their loss to Hull FC, St Helens looked down and out. With triumphant wins over Wakefield and Castleford, the never-say-die attitude has been reinstated once again.

They will now refocus and aim for three wins out of three to be in with a shout. If they win all three they move to 34 points.

Not only that, they face other teams in the play-off hunt and will take on Leeds Rhinos (H), Leigh Leopards (A) and Hull KR (H).

All three their three remaining matches are against teams in the top six - talk about having to take your moment.

Will they do the unthinkable? If they do manage to win their next two, that final-round contest against Hull KR could be extra tasty...

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tripura chief minister Manik Saha has fulfilled a promise made to Commonwealth Games gold medallist Asmita Dey, with the state government allotting her a piece of land in Agartala to build a house.The 23-year-old judoka was honoured in Tripura on Wednesday after becoming the first Indian judoka to win a Commonwealth Games gold medal.Dey won the womenâs -48kg title in Glasgow after defeating Canadaâs Heidi Quach in a dramatic golden-score contest. The state government also presented her with a cheque of Rs 10 lakh as part of the felicitation.From a village in Tripura to Commonwealth Games glorySpeaking at the event, Saha highlighted Deyâs difficult journey from a small village in South Tripura to the top of the Commonwealth Games podium. Her father, he noted, worked as a cycle mechanic in Sonaichari.âThe journey from an obscure village in South Tripura to a podium finish at Glasgow was a race against time. Her father was a cycle mechanic at Sonaichari. Against all odds, she stood firm on her mission and achieved phenomenal success for the country,â he said.The chief minister recalled meeting Dey at Tripura Bhavan in New Delhi after her return from the Games. During that meeting, the judoka had expressed her wish to have a house in Agartala.âDuring the meeting, Asmita revealed she desperately wanted a house in Agartala. I promised to fulfil her wish, and today a piece of land has been allotted to her,â he said.CM urges Asmita to target Asian Games successSaha said Deyâs achievement could motivate more young athletes from Tripura to pursue sport at the highest level. He also urged her to remain disciplined as she prepares for the Asian Games, particularly because of the strict anti-doping requirements.âI urge Asmita to remain alert, particularly about food, because she has to pass through a stringent dope test before joining the prestigious Asian Games. We believe she will shine again in the Asian Games by winning a medal for the country,â he said.Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Tinku Roy, Agartala Mayor Dipak Majumder and Arjuna award-winning gymnast Dipa Karmakar were among those who attended the felicitation ceremony.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: The Hundred 2026 awards: Stuart Broad, Nasser Hussain, Lydia Greenway pick best local player, overseas player, newcomer, fielder, captain and more
articles.summary: Nasser Hussain, Stuart Broad, Lydia Greenway pick their best local player, overseas player, newcomer, value for money, fielder, captain for 2026 Hundred season in men and women's competitions
articles.body:
Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain and Stuart Broad give out their player awards for the 2026 men's Hundred campaign, while Lydia Greenway looks at the women's competition...

Best local player

Stuart Broad:

"Jos Buttler is into the eliminator with Manchester Super Giants. Batting three, he's scored vital runs at vital times.

"He's England's best-ever white-ball batter. He's the icon of that MSG franchise.

"He's a leader in that changing room and he's got a chance of lifting the trophy."

Nasser Hussain:

"Ben Duckett went straight to the final with Trent Rockets and avoided the eliminator. That's how well he's played.

"Top of the order, he plays spin, plays fast bowling, hits it in unusual areas. He's been brilliant in the field.

"Also, at the top of the order, the way he's set the tone for that middle order of the Trent Rockets, it's just nice to see Duckett playing with such confidence and such flair.

I mentioned his fielding as well, which we do have a section on, but he's been excellent. I'm very impressed."

  • Today's cricket scorecards: The Hundred and more
  • The Hundred - latest men's and women's tables for 2026
  • Watch The Hundred and more sport contract-free on NOW

Lydia Greenway:

"I've gone for the leading wicket taker in the tournament, Tilly Corteen-Coleman. I think she's taken 13 wickets.

"The reason I picked her, she's just been really consistent. Not just this season but over the last couple of seasons.

"It's great to see her top of the tree with the wickets."

Best overseas player

Stuart Broad:

"Mitch Marsh has played some really eye-catching innings. He's batting at one of the best batting services in the country at Headingley, and he's been really entertaining.

"He's done exactly what you want an overseas player at the top of the order to do. He's led from the front. He's set the tone. He's guided his teams to win.

"His average is higher when they win than when they lose, which means he's playing a key role in winning games. Look at his strike rate, nearly 170.

"So I think he's been really crucial and a really clever signing."

Nasser Hussain:

"Mitch Marsh. Compare his consistency to someone like Harry Brook. Now, Harry's a very fine player, but a lot of his runs have come at Headingley on that belter of a surface.

"Mitch Marsh knows Headingley well, he's got Test runs there. He loves it, but he's also gone away from home at Trent Bridge, Manchester. He's got runs all around the country.

"I like the way he's a very simple person. He's a very simple player. You pitch it up, he belts it straight back past you. You drop your length back just a fraction and he'll pull you for six.

"I just love the way he keeps it very simple. And for an Aussie, he's a really nice top bloke."

Lydia Greenway:

"Overseas player has to be Phoebe Litchfield. She's obviously the leading run scorer, and the way she's gone out and dominated bowling attacks has been really entertaining to watch.

"She looks as if she's in the form of her life. She's the hardest player to set a field to in the competition.

"She hits straight down the ground, she hits behind square and then she can open up square of the wicket on both sides. She's got that ridiculous switch hit.

"If I was a captain against her, I would literally have no idea where to set the field to. She's absolutely the player in form at the moment."

Best newcomer

Nasser Hussain:

"Mitch Marsh is new to The Hundred. This is the first year he's played in The Hundred. So if he's new and he's come here from Australia, I have him as a newcomer.

"He had never played a Hundred game before this, I'm taking his age away from it."

Stuart Broad:

"I've gone for a young player who's had his first go, not in franchise cricket but in The Hundred, LD Pretorius.

"No one's really seen him in England, not really heard of him. He's not scored Ashes centuries.

"Pretorius, to me, he's playing on a difficult surface at Lord's, he's played some beautiful shots.

"He's got clear strength through the offside. A pick-up over square leg, which is fantastic.

"He's a really stylish player, and he's one of those newcomers the world of cricket will know a lot of in five years' time."

Lydia Greenway:

"I've gone for Charley Phillips. She has come in and really made the most of her opportunity. She's taken some big scalps as well within the seven wickets she's taken.

"And she's bowled in different phases of the game."

Best value for money

Nasser Hussain:

"I've gone Calvin Harrison, because he came in late as a replacement player.

"Around about £31,000 was the replacement figure. And he's bowled beautifully. He's got eight wickets.

"He's fielded really well, we've seen some of his extraordinary catches, but I just think to come in at the last moment and play, he's a real talented cricketer.

"That's someone England should be looking at across formats. He bats very well - he hasn't had much chance with the bat because the Trent Rockets have been so good - but value for money, I'm going Calvin Harrison and what he's done for the Trent Rockets."

Stuart Broad:

"I completely agree with Nasser. Calvin Harrison's been absolutely superb and now it's my time to be honest and say I've got this completely wrong with Adil Rashid, because he's on £250k to play!

"Yes, he's been very successful but as Nasser, I think, got newcomer wrong, I might have got value for money wrong because a quarter of a million pounds is quite a lot of money for eight games.

"He's been fantastic, Adil Rashid, as he was going to be.

"He's one of those players that I think every single team would have been talking about at the start of the auction. You know what you're going to get. He just delivers time after time.

"His leg spin, which is always crucial. We're in a dry spell, so it's going to spin a little bit more.

"He's one of those players that could have gone for a lot more. When you're talking about Harry Brook at £465k, Jofra Archer at £450k at the same franchise, that's where I sneaked in my value for money, because he's virtually half the price of Archer, but he performs.

Lydia Greenway:

"I've gone for Charley Phillips again here. I think she was a bargain at £15k.

"It's brilliant to see a player like her in the form that she's been in.

"And the wickets that I've mentioned, she's got big wickets. She's got Sophie Devine, Georgia Voll has been in there, Phoebe Litchfield as well, Hollie Armitage.

"So she's just been able to go in, has got quite a slingy action and just hits the top of off-stump. So it's been a pleasure to watch."

Love to watch

Nasser Hussain:

"Adil Rashid. Because in an era when spin bowlers have to bowl it quickly, have to bowl it into the surface, I still love the fact that Adil Rashid is brave enough to toss the ball up with all the variations.

articles.title: Super League receive investment offer from Australia's National Rugby League as part of 'recapitalisation project'
articles.summary: Super League have received an investment offer from Australia Rugby League Commission (ARLC) who run the NRL; Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season - including two matches in each round exclusively live
articles.body:
Super League have received an investment offer from the Australia Rugby League Commission (ARLC) which governs the National Rugby League (NRL) in Australia.

Conversations have long been occurring between Australia's governing body and Europe's, with a formal offer now having been received.

In a statement, Super League said: "RL Commercial can confirm that a first offer has been received from the ARLC (Australian Rugby League Commission) as part of the sport's recapitalisation project.

  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want
  • Listen to The Bench, Sky's rugby league podcast

"The Super League clubs have been informed this morning.

"Details of the offer remain confidential."

Former NRL chief executive Andrew Abdo spoke to Sky Sports back in April about the NRL's planned involvement in Super League. He was over in the UK for talks about the move.

He said it was a move focused on the "globalisation" of rugby league with a view to ensure that rugby league in the UK and Europe is governed by an independent commission, similar to the set up of the ARLC.

ARLC Chairman Peter V'Landys is now understood to be leading the talks.

"We really believe in the globalisation of rugby league," Abdo told Sky Sports.

"This is a great game and we want to take it to as many people as possible. We want to win as many fans as possible.

"So while the game is growing really well in the southern hemisphere, we also want the game to be strong here in the north.

"This is about a partnership where we can collaborate on how we can grow the game, how we can grow revenues and how can those revenues be pumped back into the game?

"That's pretty nuanced and that's something we have to develop together."

RL Commercial managing director Rhodri Jones added on the talks from April: "They would like to have a heavy influence on the commission and who sits on that commission.

"What they perhaps haven't understood in totality is the make up of our governance structure in this country.

"We have multiple organisations in RFL, Super League and RL Commercial. When it is such a big topic like recapitalisation, it is complex.

"But with hard work, better detail, we can overcome some of these challenges so we can get to the right result that the sport wants."

The talks have now moved into the next negotiation phase.

2026 Super League - key dates and what to look out for

  • Elimination Play-offs: September 19-September 20
  • Play-off semi-finals: September 26-September 27
  • Grand Final: October 3, Old Trafford.

Sky Sports will again show every game of the Super League live this season - including two matches in each round exclusively live, with the remaining five matches each week shown on Sky Sports+

articles.title: Super League: Coach-less Castleford Tigers claim much-needed victory at Hull FC with Ryan Carr still absent
articles.summary: Liam Hood strikes decisive late try as Castleford Tigers claim much-needed Super League victory at Hull FC on Friday night; win comes with Tigers head coach Ryan Carr still absent for personal reasons; Castleford arrest run of three straight losses in which they conceded 144 points
articles.body:
Castleford Tigers ended a disastrous run in Super League with a late 18-14 win at Hull FC on Friday.

The Tigers had conceded 144 points in successive defeats to Wakefield, Warrington and Hull KR but bounced back at the MKM Stadium thanks to Liam Hood's late try.

Castleford - whose head coach Ryan Carr remains absent for personal reasons - opened the scoring after 10 minutes when Renouf Atoni took a short ball at speed and Tom Weaver added the conversion

  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want
  • Listen to The Bench, Sky's rugby league podcast

Mikaele Ravalawa dived over to stretch the lead after Phoenix Laulu-Togagae had lofted a perfectly-weighted pass into the corner.

Weaver kicked a penalty to make it 12-0 but Hull launched a stirring fightback either side of the interval.

Jakob Arthur's grubber kick was collected by Joe Batchelor and Aidan Sezer added the goal.

Hull claimed the lead as Harvey Barron took a high ball to touch down and Sezer sent over Lewis Martin in the corner.

But Hood burst over from dummy-half 12 minutes from time and Weaver enjoyed more kicking success as the Tigers climbed two places to ninth while Hull stay 12th.

Castleford Director of Rugby Chester: It's been turbulent - I don't know what situation is, the board will make call

Castleford Tigers Director of Rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports:

"I'm not too sure [what the situation with Ryan Carr is]. My focus this week and certainly over the last few days has been getting these guys ready for a tough game against Hull FC.

"It's been a really turbulent week.

"The board will make that decision when it's right. My job has been to prepare these guys the best I possibly could and they showed some real heart out there and played for the badge tonight.

"But I just want to say a few words on Danny Wilson [Castleford chief executive], who is laid up in bed, he hasn't been well. We miss him here at the club.

"That win was for him."

articles.title: Super League: St Helens keep slim play-off hopes alive after stirring second half earns 46-16 win over Wakefield Trinity
articles.summary: St Helens have never failed to make play-offs but in battle to reach post-season this year; Saints bounce back from three straight defeats with victory at Wakefield after 34 unanswered points in second half; Wigan beat Bradford, who drop to foot of table after Huddersfield win at Toulouse
articles.body:
St Helens produced a blistering second-half performance to stun Wakefield Trinity with a 46-16 victory and keep their slim Super League play-off hopes alive.

Saints, who have never failed to make the post-season, came into the match on a run of three defeats in a row and five losses in six, leaving them six points off the top six.

The visitors slipped 10-0 down to fourth-placed Wakefield and trailed 16-12 at half-time but then ran in six unanswered tries in the second period.

Tristan Sailor's brace completed his hat-trick while Lewis Murphy added to his first-half score and Jake Davies touched down twice in the closing stages to move St Helens to within four points of sixth-placed Leigh Leopards with four games remaining.

Wakefield falter after bright start

Wakefield, who lost Josh Rourke and try-scorer Isaiah Vagana to injuries inside the first quarter of an hour, missed the chance to move two points behind table toppers Leeds as they suffered a sixth successive defeat to Saints and slipped to back-to-back home losses after last week's narrow reverse against the Rhinos.

articles.title: The Hundred: Tim Seifert propels Manchester Super Giants to title with last-gasp win over Trent Rockets in Lord's final
articles.summary: Tim Seifert produced a sensational 72 off 38 in the men's Hundred final at Lord's; Liam Dawson smashed a six over the rope to win the title with two balls to go; Rockets miss out on a clean sweep of men's and women's titles
articles.body:
Tim Seifert produced an imperious 72 off 38 balls to steer the Manchester Super Giants to The Hundred title after a five-wicket victory over the Trent Rockets in an incredible final at Lord's that went down to the last three balls.

The opener notched the fastest fifty in men's Hundred final history and was aided by cameos from opening partner Paul Walter (22 off 14), captain Jos Buttler (23 off 14) and a crucial knock from Leus Du Plooy (27no off 18) to chase down their opponents' substantial score of 158.

Two late wickets from Mohammed Amir (3-29) gave the Rockets hope, leaving the Super Giants needing three runs off the last five balls, but spinner Liam Dawson resisted the pressure and smashed a six with three balls to go to seal the title for MSG.

  • Scorecard: Manchester Super Giants vs Trent Rockets
  • Latest Sky Sports deals or stream cricket with no contract
  • Listen to latest episode of the Sky Sports Cricket podcast

The victory secured the Super Giants their maiden Hundred title after beating SunRisers Leeds in the eliminator on Friday, preventing the Rockets from becoming the first team to win both the men's and women's Hundred after Trent Rockets women demolished SunRisers Leeds women earlier on Sunday.

Super Giants' batters storm to title-clinching victory

Rockets openers Duckett (31 off 24) and Allen (15 off 13) - who were afflicted by the low-scoring Lord's pitch, which has seen a first-innings average of just 141 during the 2026 Hundred - managed just 33 from the powerplay but seemed to have settled into their innings before Super Giants spinner Noor Ahmad (3-33) dismissed both openers in a game-changing four deliveries that took the Rockets from 48-0 to 52-2.

The batting side, though, rebounded through the impressive innings of Anuerin Donald (38 off 19), before a spell of three wickets in 11 balls - including a comedic run out that saw the captain Sam Billings dismissed - left them reeling at 95-5.

Useful cameos from Lewis Gregory (32 off 16) and Mitch Santner (20no off 16), though, helped the Rockets to a defendable score of 158 after their 100 balls.

Super Giants openers Seifert and Walter (22 off 14) - the latter of whom smashed 80 off 46 balls in the eliminator - gave their side a brilliant start to the run chase, notching their fifty partnership off just 26 balls.

Seifert was spared his blushes after an incredible one-handed diving Finn Allen catch was overruled by the third umpire after his foot brushed the boundary rope, but his partner Walter was sent packing just three deliveries later when he was caught on the boundary by Duckett to end the 66-run opening wicket stand.

Seifert, undeterred, continued his stellar innings and raced to a stunning 24-ball fifty, combining effectively with both Buttler and Du Plooy before his dismissal, but the wickets of Heinrich Klaasen (11 off 9) and Michael Bracewell (0 off 2) in successive balls to Amir set up a tantalising finale, with the Super Giants needing three off Ben Sanderson's last five balls.

Two dots in the first two balls of the last five increased the tension and pressure on tail-ender Dawson, but the England international resisted and smashed the game-winning maximum with the next ball to win the title for his side and cap off the 2026 Hundred.

Buttler: We deserved Hundred title

Manchester Super Giants captain Jos Buttler, speaking to Sky Sports:

"Mixture of emotions - the excitement and euphoria of winning it, a little bit of relief after the last few balls there - but fantastic effort from everyone to lift the trophy. I think we deserve it.

"I enjoyed [captaining]. It's a little bit more stressful, but captaining a great bunch of guys with a bowling attack that's really varied.

"It was crucial that we broke some really important partnerships and that went a long way to winning the game.

"We've had some brilliant performances from everyone. The two boys at the top of the order since Aiden [Markram] hasn't been here have been outstanding - but it's also been the wicket-taking ability,

"We're very well-marshalled off the field by a great coaching team as well. Tom Moody, Justin Langer and everyone have been brilliant - I'm proud of everyone involved."

articles.title: The Hundred: Trent Rockets thrash SunRisers Leeds at Lord's to win women's title for first time
articles.summary: Defending women's Hundred champions SunRisers Leeds skittled for 91 by Trent Rockets in women's final; Georgia Adams stars with ball and in field for Rockets, before Ash Gardner's side ease to target in just 54 balls; Rockets won eight of their nine games this season, including last seven
articles.body:
Trent Rockets stormed to a first women's Hundred title after demolishing defending champions SunRisers Leeds by eight wickets in a one-sided final at Lord's.

Rockets razed SunRisers for 91 from as many balls after winning the toss before cantering to their target with 46 deliveries to spare as skipper Ash Gardner pounded the winning four through the off-side.

Georgia Adams (2-15 from nine balls), playing in her fifth Hundred final, enjoyed a brilliant afternoon for Rockets.

  • Scorecard: Trent Rockets Women vs Sunrisers Leeds Women
  • Latest Sky Sports deals or stream cricket with no contract
  • Listen to latest episode of the Sky Sports Cricket podcast

The off-spinning all-rounder's wickets included Annabel Sutherland (25) stumped, while she also caught the dangerous Phoebe Litchfield (10) at short fine leg on the scoop and superbly ran out Jess Jonassen (0) from cover.

Rockets made light work of the chase with Sophia Dunkley (41 off 23) and Beth Mooney (31no off 21) pounding 45 in the 25-ball powerplay during an opening stand of 69 from 61 balls - Dunkley looked on course for fourth fifty of the campaign before spooning Dani Gibson to short cover with 23 runs needed.

Sutherland and SunRisers skipper Gibson (22) were the only batters in their side to make it into the 20s, with the team slumping to 24-3 after 19 balls and then losing their final seven wickets for 35 once Deepti Sharma (12) was bowled.

Rockets romp to victory as bowlers set the tone

Rockets, who secured a seventh win in a row and an eighth in nine overall, were clinical with the ball, starting with Kim Garth (2-18) striking twice in as many legal deliveries early on to banish Bryony Smith (2) and birthday girl Lauren Winfield-Hill (0).

Charley Phillips (2-12) and Samantha Bates (2-17) also picked up a brace of wickets for Rockets, with Bates' haul taking her to 13 in the tournament.

Sutherland and Gibson added fleeting impetus for SunRisers - the former clubbing the only six of the innings and the latter latching on to some wayward deliveries from Garth - but there was little else to cheer for the team in orange.

SunRisers' triumph last summer, which came under their previous Northern Superchargers name, saw them upset table toppers Southern Brave in the final.

But they could not repeat that result against this year's winners of the league phase as they lost to Rockets for a second time this season, following a five-run loss at Trent Bridge on August 2.

That was a slender defeat, this was a hammering, with perhaps the only disappointment for Rockets that Nat Sciver-Brunt fell cheaply, pinned lbw by Sutherland for four.

'Adams turns up in big games'

Sky Sports Cricket's Nasser Hussain:

"Georgia Adams is a serial winner, a top signing, she turned the game around.

"It's not just about the wickets and catches, it's about who you get out. Annabel Sutherland, Phoebe Litchfield, Jess Jonassen. That was a serious performance from someone who consistently turns up in the big games."

'We aren't reliant on one or two people'

Rockets captain Ash Gardner:

"Different people stood up at different times. It's been a fantastic campaign to be part of. I've said it all along, we're not reliant on one or two people.

"People played their role, that is all you can ask as a captain. We've been fantastic throughout. We're an experienced group and I've been able to lean on many people so it hasn't just been me."

articles.title: Hull KR 28-34 Warrington Wolves: George Williams stars as Sam Burgess' side move two points off Super League top spot
articles.summary: Warrington Wolves' win puts them two points behind Leeds and Wigan; Mikey Lewis was sent to the sin bin on the return from his four-match ban for dangerous contact with kicker Ewan Irwin; round 24 of Super League continues on Thursday August 20, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Warrington Wolves sent a statement with a 34-28 win over Hull KR in their rearranged Super League round two match at Sewell Group Craven Park.

The match could not take place 22 rounds ago due to the Robins being in Las Vegas but the new allotted time seemed to suit Sam Burgess' side as they romped to a victory which puts them two points off top spot.

For the home side, the stand out point will be that Mikey Lewis returned from a four-game ban, in which they won all four matches, but then was sin-binned in a contest in which they were second best.

  • Super League's Final Charge: Seven teams in contention
  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want

The yellow card came for a dangerous contact with kicker Ewan Irwin, which Warrington head coach Sam Burgess described as "dangerous".

"I think the challenge at the back end of the game was a bad challenge. It is a bad challenge. He (Irwin) is very lucky he's come out of that healthy. He's a tough kid," Burgess said.

"I'm not trying to make it worse than it is.," he later added. "You just have to watch it. It's really dangerous.
In the NRL, you're going to be in a bit of trouble."

The Robins did have a 14-10 half-time lead thanks to a Rhyse Martin penalty plus converted Lewis and Karl Lawton tries.

Warrington went over through an unconverted Albert Hopoate effort and a James Bentley try, but were four points adrift.

But a dominant second half saw Toafofa Sipley, Liam Byrne, George Williams and Albert Hopoate all score, ensuring late tries from Dean Hadley and Tevita Pangai Jnr were sheer consolations, while Mikey Lewis was sin-binned on his return from suspension.

Wolves show play-off credentials

Hull KR took an early lead through the boot of Martin after Warrington conceded a penalty for a high shot on Frenchman Arthur Mourgue.

But the Robins started to make errors, twice dropping the ball and then conceding a penalty. Warrington slowly turned the screw and after forcing three repeat sets, they eventually scored the first try of the game as a sweeping move from left to right saw Hopoate squeeze home in the corner on 18 minutes.

Irwin couldn't convert, and it was the Wire who came up with errors for the next period. However, the hosts didn't punish them and when they eventually conceded a penalty for holding down, England captain Williams produced a crisp pass for Bentley to race on to and score from close range, Irwin tagging on the extras this time for a 10-2 lead.

But Rovers were ahead before the break. On his return from a four-match suspension, Lewis got himself on the scoresheet after being the first to react to Jez Litten's threaded kick to the in-goal, and a minute before the break Lawton barged over, with both tries converted by Mourgue.

That put Rovers 14-10 ahead, but Sam Burgess' side were ahead three minutes after the interval as powerhouse prop Sipley crashed over from a few meters out after Danny Walker's smart pass, with Irwin converting once again.

On 50 minutes, Mourgue brought the game level with a penalty goal, leaving the game evenly poised at a crucial period.

The game would soon be injected with further spice as a commotion saw players from both teams come together.

But the Robins lost their composure as Mourgue was penalised for a needless block on Walker while his team were coming away from their own try line. That allowed Irwin to kick a penalty goal to go two points ahead once again.

Immediately after that, Lewis kicked out on the full for the second time in the game and Warrington made the most of it once more, with Byrne smashing through the defensive line to score a converted try that extended the lead to eight points going into the final quarter.

From there, it was one-way traffic. The brilliant Williams got on the inside of Litten to score by the sticks, and he then produced a wonderful kick that was sublimely finished by Hopoate to add emphasis to the scoreline.

Hadley and Pangai Jr got late consolations for Rovers, but it was too little, too late.

Burgess: Scoreline doesn't reflect dominance

Player of the match George Williams told Sky Sports:

"For Mikey Lewis, he's a nice quiet lad, not how he plays. It's a fine line, and at the minute he's getting it wrong. But just put an arm around him.

"He's one of the best players in the comp."

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess:

"I'm happy and proud of the team. We didn't have it our way for parts of it.

"We'll reassess, but I'm proud of the spirit. This is a tough place to come.

"I'm proud of our effort and physicality.

"The scoreline didn't reflect the game in the first half, and it's fair to say it doesn't in the second half either. We were dominant in a lot of areas.

"Our collective effort, everyone did their jobs. We grew in the disruption."

Peters: Warrington didn't have to work for tries

Hull KR head coach Willie Peters to Sky Sports:

"Yeah it was a tough second half to watch.

"There were a lot of moments to like in that game, but a lot we won't want to watch back again. Just not good enough.

"It's disappointing and I'm disappointed with the tries we let in.

"Warrington are a very good team, I'm not taking anything away from them, but they didn't have to work for coming through the middle of us.

"We're a brave team, because it could have got worse, but obviously the game was gone by the end.

"I need to have a look at the Mikey Lewis incident. I don't know how bad it was."

However, the hosts didn't punish them and when they eventually conceded a penalty for holding down, England captain Williams produced a crisp pass for Bentley to race on to and score from close range, Irwin tagging on the extras this time for a 10-2 lead.

But Rovers were ahead before the break. On his return from a four-match suspension, Lewis got himself on the scoresheet after being the first to react to Jez Litten's threaded kick to the in-goal, and a minute before the break Lawton barged over, with both tries converted by Mourgue.

That put Rovers 14-10 ahead, but Sam Burgess' side were ahead three minutes after the interval as powerhouse prop Sipley crashed over from a few meters out after Danny Walker's smart pass, with Irwin converting once again.

On 50 minutes, Mourgue brought the game level with a penalty goal, leaving the game evenly poised at a crucial period.

The game would soon be injected with further spice as a commotion saw players from both teams come together.

But the Robins lost their composure as Mourgue was penalised for a needless block on Walker while his team were coming away from their own try line. That allowed Irwin to kick a penalty goal to go two points ahead once again.

Immediately after that, Lewis kicked out on the full for the second time in the game and Warrington made the most of it once more, with Byrne smashing through the defensive line to score a converted try that extended the lead to eight points going into the final quarter.

From there, it was one-way traffic. The brilliant Williams got on the inside of Litten to score by the sticks, and he then produced a wonderful kick that was sublimely finished by Hopoate to add emphasis to the scoreline.

Hadley and Pangai Jr got late consolations for Rovers, but it was too little, too late.

Burgess: Scoreline doesn't reflect dominance

Player of the match George Williams told Sky Sports:

"For Mikey Lewis, he's a nice quiet lad, not how he plays. It's a fine line, and at the minute he's getting it wrong. But just put an arm around him.

"He's one of the best players in the comp."

Warrington Wolves head coach Sam Burgess:

"I'm happy and proud of the team. We didn't have it our way for parts of it.

"We'll reassess, but I'm proud of the spirit. This is a tough place to come.

"I'm proud of our effort and physicality.

"The scoreline didn't reflect the game in the first half, and it's fair to say it doesn't in the second half either. We were dominant in a lot of areas.

"Our collective effort, everyone did their jobs. We grew in the disruption."

Peters: Warrington didn't have to work for tries

Hull KR head coach Willie Peters to Sky Sports:

"Yeah it was a tough second half to watch.

"There were a lot of moments to like in that game, but a lot we won't want to watch back again. Just not good enough.

"It's disappointing and I'm disappointed with the tries we let in.

"Warrington are a very good team, I'm not taking anything away from them, but they didn't have to work for coming through the middle of us.

"We're a brave team, because it could have got worse, but obviously the game was gone by the end.

"I need to have a look at the Mikey Lewis incident. I don't know how bad it was."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

articles.title: Patrick Kane Throws Out Cubs 1st Pitch in Trending Video After Return to Blackhawks on New Contract
articles.summary: Patrick Kane got a warm welcome back to Chicago after rejoining the Chicago Blackhawks last month.
articles.body:
Patrick Kane got a warm welcome back to Chicago after rejoining the Chicago Blackhawks last month.

The veteran right winger threw out the first pitch at Wrigley Field ahead of Tuesday night's matchup between the Cubs and White Sox.

Kane, 37, agreed to a two-year, $8 million contract with the Blackhawks to set up a reunion between him and the team where he had the best years of his career. He played for Chicago from 2007 to 2023, winning a Hart Trophy and three Stanley Cups

The Blackhawks traded Kane to the Detroit Red Wings at the deadline in 2023 as they began shifting towards a rebuild. He played the last three seasons in Detroit on one-year deals.

When Kane decided to return for a 20th NHL season, rejoining the Blackhawks seemed like a perfect move, and now he's back with the team that drafted him first overall nearly two decades ago.

"What a time! To say I get to be a Blackhawk again is an amazing feeling... the love, passion and energy I've felt from the fans has been unparalleled, even when I was not always wearing the Blackhawks sweater," Kane wrote in a social media post after signing his new deal. "There's nothing like the city of Chicago and home games in the UC."

Kane is coming off a season in which he recorded 57 points (16 goals, 41 assists) in 67 games. He'll look to put together a strong year as the Blackhawks try to get back to the playoffs for the first time since 2020.

Having a franchise legend like Kane should help the young, rebuilding squad progress this year.

articles.title: 5 Potential Kenny Omega vs. Will Ospreay Outcomes at AEW All In 2026
articles.summary: The main event of All In on August 30 will see Will Ospreay challenge Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship.
articles.body:
The main event of All In on August 30 will see Will Ospreay challenge Kenny Omega for the AEW World Championship.

For many fans, the outcome seems predictable, but there are several ways we could get to that outcome, and a few possible swerves that could turn things the other way.

This feud has been built up more than any other storyline on the card. Ospreay has been tied to Omega since he debuted with the company, and this feels like their years of history coming to a head.

The Billy Goat will have the home-crowd advantage at Wembley Stadium in London, but Omega seems determined to prove he is the better man.

Let's look at some of the possible outcomes for this match.

If you're a fan of Ospreay, the best possible outcome would be him defeating Omega clean in the middle of the ring to win the belt.

It would be the most satisfying conclusion for a lot of people because it would put all of the focus on Ospreay for his big moment in front of his countrymen in England.

However, some fans will also find this to be one of the most boring possible outcomes because it seems so predictable. It feels like all of this has been set up to put the belt on Ospreay, and if that is what happens, some people might think it was so obvious that AEW should have swerved us instead.

Sadly, you can't please everyone, but if you're a fan of The Billy Goat, you probably want this ending.

A lot of people think Ospreay winning is a foregone conclusion, but there is always the possibility that Tony Khan wants to go a different direction.

Omega winning cleanly would be the most surprising ending to this match, and that is one big reason why it might happen. As exciting as All Elite Wrestling's action can be, it can also be rather predictable with results, so shocking everyone is not out of the question.

AEW has generally favored longer world-title reigns, and with Omega having won the belt only on July 8 after the previous two champions had relatively short reigns, Khan may want to give him a longer run.

The Cleaner hitting the One-Winged Angel to score the win might not go over well in England, but it would make a lot of fans in the U.S. happy.

Part of Ospreay's story with The Death Riders was about Jon Moxley attempting to get him to cross lines he was unwilling to cross, and that eventually led to him cutting ties with Mox and his crew.

But what if Ospreay is willing to get his hands dirty in a different way? He has already said he is calling some of his United Empire buddies, so even if he doesn't try to end Omega's career, he might use his friends to win.

The biggest problem with this outcome is that it would negate a lot of the progress Ospreay made when choosing not to put the plastic bag over Kenny's head.

Turning him heel now wouldn't make a lot of sense, and it would taint his first world title victory for a lot of British fans who will be watching from the stands. That is why this outcome, while possible, is a lot less likely to happen.

The odds of a full heel turn for Omega seem slim, but there is one way this match might end that sees him win due to outside interference.

Ospreay turned on Moxley and The Death Riders leading up to this match, so if Mox wants a little payback, he might see costing Ospreay the title as his best option.

This would allow AEW to keep the belt on Omega for a bit while kicking off a full Moxley vs. Ospreay feud at the same time, which is going to happen eventually anyway.

A dirty finish to a main event is never ideal, but this is one of the times when it would make sense for storytelling purposes. Moxley might even succeed in making The Billy Goat cross his own boundaries by making him too angry to keep his cool after the loss.

An Ospreay who is at the end of his rope and wants revenge might even be more interesting than having him win the world title at this point.

The Death Riders getting involved not only creates the possibility of Omega retaining, but it could also lead to neither man actually winning.

Imagine this. Ospreay and Omega have a great back-and-forth match that feels like it's building to the finish, and then Moxley and his cohorts appear to destroy both men.

This would definitely be the least popular outcome proposed in this article, but this is pro wrestling, so all things are possible until a decision is made by management.

Having Mox take out both men and declare his intentions to regain the title would put Ospreay and Omega back on the same side temporarily. It could even lead to The Billy Goat teaming up with The Elite to battle The Death Riders in one of AEW's big stipulations like Stadium Stampede or Blood and Guts.

This wouldn't be a satisfying conclusion to All In, but we have to consider it as a possibility.

How do you think Ospreay vs. Omega will end at All In?

articles.title: Adam 'Edge' Copeland Reveals WWE Denied John Cena's Retirement Match Following Rumors amid AEW Run
articles.summary: During John Cena's retirement tour last year in which he stepped in the ring with many of his past WWE rivals, one name missing from the group was Edge in part because he had left to join AEW back in 2023.
articles.body:
During John Cena's retirement tour last year in which he stepped in the ring with many of his past WWE rivals, one name missing from the group was Edge in part because he had left to join AEW back in 2023.

Appearing on The Ariel Helwani Show , Adam Copeland was asked about the rumors he might have been the one to show up as Cena's final opponent last December.

The most interesting nugget is Copeland saying AEW president Tony Khan "absolutely" would have allowed him to do it, but he "never pursued" it knowing WWE would never consider it.

Copeland did note his original AEW contract might have expired in time for him to make a return appearance in WWE last year, but his time off due to injuries and film projects extended his tenure. He also made it clear he intends to spend the rest of his career with AEW.

"Yes. Yeah. That's where I want to," he said about ending his career in AEW. "I know that may disappoint a lot of people, but I love it there."

Appearing on Helwani's show last November (h/t Ethan Schlabaugh of SI.com), Khan confirmed WWE never reached out about letting Copeland wrestle Cena at some point during the latter's retirement run.

Even though one last Cena-Edge match never occurred, the two did pay tribute to each other in matches last year.

The onscreen rivalry between Edge and Cena throughout the mid-2000s was instrumental in elevating both men to superstardom. Cena was already on his way there, but Edge got a huge boost from the feud.

Edge won his first singles world title in WWE by defeating Cena at New Year's Revolution in January 2006 when he cashed in his Money in the Bank briefcase that he won the previous year at WrestleMania.

Cena and Copeland wrestled against each other 62 times , either in singles, tag or multi-person matches, in WWE.

The Rated R Superstar went on to become an 11-time WWE/world heavyweight champion before departing the company in 2023.

Since debuting in AEW, Copeland has primarily been paired with Christian Cage. The duo won the AEW tag team titles by defeating FTR in an I Quit match at Double or Nothing in May.

Copeland and Cage are next set to defend the championships against the Young Bucks at All In on Aug. 30.

articles.title: Panthers' Brad Marchand Trolls Maple Leafs' William Nylander Over Workout Photo
articles.summary: A potentially delayed start to the 2026-27 season hasn't stopped Florida Panthers star Brad Marchand from chirping his future opponents.
articles.body:
A potentially delayed start to the 2026-27 season hasn't stopped Florida Panthers star Brad Marchand from chirping his future opponents.

Marchand responded Tuesday to a photo shared on the NHL's Instagram of the Toronto Maple Leafs' William Nylander lifting.

"Don't hurt yourself with all that weight willy," Marchand wrote.

Marchand recently said in a video posted to social media he had undergone offseason surgery.

The forward was sidelined for the end of the 2025-26 season with something head coach Paul Maurice said he had been dealing with "for a couple of months."

Marchand said in a video posted earlier this month he had been trying to treat the issue without surgery but ultimately "had to kind of do it last minute."

It is not clear when Marchand will be able to rejoin the Panthers, which are set to open training camp within the next month prior to opening the regular season Sept. 29 against the defending Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes.

The Panthers will hope to have him back in the lineup by the time the team faces Nylander and the Leafs on Dec. 3 in Toronto.

articles.title: Supplements: what do athletes take and why?
articles.summary: There is a long list of supplements taken by elite athletes in the pursuit of marginal gains - what do they take and why?
articles.body:
It was at the 1992 Olympics in Barcelona when the mutterings about a new "secret weapon" started.

Dozens of Great Britain athletes had been taking a new product that increased muscle mass and improved athletic performance â a "wonder pill" that didn't fall foul of any doping rules.

Now found in tubs and bags on many supermarket shelves and tagged in your social feeds, it is the supplement of choice for millions of people and one of the most scientifically researched.

But back then, when it came on the scene at the very top of British elite sport, there were suspicions and stigma around the use of any substance described as 'performance enhancing' â even if it was legal.

From the minute an athlete wakes, to the moment they go to bed, they are thinking about how they can optimise their performance and recovery.

Today, creatine is just one of a long list of supplements taken by elite athletes in this pursuit of marginal gains. Some help with muscle size and strength, while others correct deficiencies in the diet.

"There are various reports in the literature of some studies that say maybe up to 90% of athletes take supplements. I often jokingly say that means 10% are lying," says Prof Graeme Close, professor of human physiology at Liverpool John Moores University.

"The sports teams that I've worked in, I think that's probably closer to 100% of athletes will be taking some form of supplementation."

So, what do supplements actually do and why do athletes take them? And in the world of strict liability, where elite athletes are solely responsible for what they put in their bodies, how do they make sure they stay clean?

While experts like Close advocate for seeking to meet nutritional needs through food in the first instance, it may not always be possible or practical to do this - and that is where supplements come in.

Take, for example, creatine, which is found naturally in meat and fish.

"You would need the best part of a kilogram of raw chicken a day to get the amount of creatine you need," says Close. But it is unsafe to eat raw poultry because of the food poisoning risk from harmful bacteria.

Creatine is a natural compound in the body produced in the kidneys, liver and pancreas. It is a quick source of energy for muscles, which is especially important for short-duration, high intensity activities such as sprinting.

Its big break as a supplement came in the 1990s when two scientists who had been researching it for two decades shared their findings with Steve Jennings, whose Maxim sports nutrition company supplied products to the British Olympic team.

During the 1992 Barcelona Games, investigative reporter Doug Gillon had learned of a 'secret trial' involving British athletes and seen a box of their Ergomax C150 â effervescent creatine tablets. He wrote that if the scientists' claims - that creatine could improve explosive athletic performance by 1-3% - were true, then "sport may never be the same again".

In terms of sport supplements and nutrition, he was right. By the time of the next Olympics in 1996, an estimated 80% of athletes were taking creatine, and since then it has become mainstream, with research suggesting there may be cognitive benefits as well as physical.

According to the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, the creatine breakthrough of the 1990s had "launched a new era in sports nutrition" and "sparked exploration into other supplements".

The global dietary supplements market size was valued at $209.5bn (Â£154bn) in 2025 and is projected to grow to $431.7bn (Â£317.4bn) by 2033, according to Grand View Research. , external

Close, who oversaw nutrition for last year's British and Irish Lions rugby union tour, sees supplements as the "final piece of the jigsaw" rather than a starting point.

"What we're talking about is small margins of benefit, where actually these athletes who focus on the food, I think what you often find is that they've got the big-ticket items right," he says.

"So they're seeing great performance benefits because their overall diet is immaculate.

"They might be missing out on the one per-centers, but they've really nailed the 99 per-centers. And they often do better than those who chase the one per-centers but have not given enough attention to the 99 per-centers."

Australian cyclist Nicole Frain agrees, adding: "I'm a pretty big believer that they are called sport supplements. They are there to supplement the things you already do right.

"I don't think supplements are the answer to fix my problems.

"You need to be eating a balanced diet, training well, sleeping right, recovering well, hydrating â all of those things â before we add in all of the extras."

Close puts protein powders top of the list of supplements taken by athletes he works with, followed by creatine and vitamin D.

Protein powders maximise muscle repair and contribute to muscle growth, while creatine is a quick source of energy for muscles and important in short-duration, high-intensity activities like sprinting. Vitamin D, meanwhile, is essential for bone health and supports muscle function.

Other popular supplements include carbohydrate gels, which Close says were key in the first sub-two hour marathon run earlier this year by Kenyan long-distance runner Sabastian Sawe.

"As sport nutritionists we were all fascinated at what the fuelling programme was, and it was the sports drinks and gels that played a huge part of that fuelling," Close says.

"There was a calculation done of what it would take to break the two-hour marathon, and that did involve making sure that over 100 grams of supplemental carbohydrate were ingested per hour.

"And the reports coming out of the recent sub-two-hour marathon was that it was 110 grams of carbohydrate per hour that was achieved."

Supplements can improve performance, but there is an uneasy ring to describing them as 'performance enhancing' because of the association with banned substances and anti-doping rule violations.

So what determines whether something is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's (Wada) banned list?

"For Wada to put anything on the list, it's got to hit two out of three criteria: dangerous to health, performance enhancing, and against the spirit of sport," Close explains.

"So just because something enhances performance, if it's not dangerous to health and not against the spirit of sport, Wada will not touch it.

"Though something like an anabolic steroid, where it's against the spirit of sport to be injecting yourself for a performance benefit, it's dangerous to health and it's performance enhancing - that hits all three."

But taking a supplement still carries anti-doping risks.

"No guarantee can be given that any particular supplement is free from prohibited substances," UK Anti-Doping advice states, urging athletes to "be vigilant" in using them.

And if you test positive for a prohibited substance, consuming it unintentionally can result in the same four-year ban as if you deliberately took it.

There are supplement-testing programmes which batch test products before they are sold to make sure they do not contain any Wada-prohibited substances.

One of those is Informed Sport, which says as many as one in 10 supplements is contaminated with ingredients and compounds prohibited in sport and points to a study carried out by the Anti-Doping Knowledge Centre that showed product contamination was responsible for 8% of all anti-doping violations between 2005 and 2022.

While Informed Sport is a very well used system among athletes, Wada makes it clear that quality assurance schemes can reduce but do not eliminate the risk of an anti-doping infringement.

If you do accept the risk, you need to be organised to keep track.

In the case of Great Britain rower Heidi Long, it takes a spreadsheet.

"I've recorded the batch number of every product that I've taken and its expiry date because if you take it after the expiry date the Informed Sport [certification] is no longer viable," she says.

Close says he has also done site visits to factories to see where the supplements are made to check the manufacturing processes because "the risk of failing a drugs test is huge".

There are risks to the general population too, he adds, saying: "You can be buying supplements off the internet that are made in somebody's garage and you've got no idea of the manufacturing processes."

He points to studies on creatine products which have found there is no creatine in them and so "you're completely wasting your money" and that in the worst case scenario it may contain substances that are dangerous to your health.

"So it is really important that the message is that while they can play a small role, the safety considerations are the key factor," he says.

There is, however, more than one way for an elite athlete to chase a competitive edge â and some are going back to basics.

For every trending supplement, there is an unprocessed, wholefood alternative â from the anti-inflammatory benefits of turmeric, staving off cramp with pickle juice or consumption of high-nitrate foods like beetroot before competition.

It is what Close calls a "food-first" or "food-only" approach and something he says every athlete should use as a starting point.

The latest to have its moment in the spotlight is an ancient Ethiopian grain called teff.

Used for thousands of years in traditional east African diets, teff is now making its mark globally in performance nutrition.

In comparison to other popular grains like wheat, rice and quinoa, teff has a high mineral content and is rich in calcium, iron and vitamin C. Naturally gluten-free and good for the gut, it is also unique for being a 'complete' protein, meaning it provides all nine essential amino acids required for human nutrition.

These superfood credentials have caught the attention of some of the world's best athletes over the years, from Olympic champion marathon runner Haile Gebrselassie to seven-time Grand Slam singles champion Venus Williams, and it is now becoming a more common sight on UK supermarket shelves.

British boxer Fran Hennessy was introduced to teff by her nutritionist and it is now part of her daily routine.

"I've never looked back," she says. "What I'm putting in my body is good fuel and energy and teff has so much. It energises you so much before a workout and it gives you the fibre you need."

As well as boosting her performances, Hennessy credits teff with being key to recovery.

Dozens of Great Britain athletes had been taking a new product that increased muscle mass and improved athletic performance â a "wonder pill" that didn't fall foul of any doping rules.
Now found in tubs and bags on many supermarket shelves and tagged in your social feeds, it is the supplement of choice for millions of people and one of the most scientifically researched.

But back then, when it came on the scene at the very top of British elite sport, there were suspicions and stigma around the use of any substance described as 'performance enhancing' â even if it was legal.

"I don't think supplements are the answer to fix my problems.
"You need to be eating a balanced diet, training well, sleeping right, recovering well, hydrating â all of those things â before we add in all of the extras."

"There was a calculation done of what it would take to break the two-hour marathon, and that did involve making sure that over 100 grams of supplemental carbohydrate were ingested per hour.

Supplements can improve performance, but there is an uneasy ring to describing them as 'performance enhancing' because of the association with banned substances and anti-doping rule violations.
So what determines whether something is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's (Wada) banned list?
"For Wada to put anything on the list, it's got to hit two out of three criteria: dangerous to health, performance enhancing, and against the spirit of sport," Close explains.

"No guarantee can be given that any particular supplement is free from prohibited substances," UK Anti-Doping advice states, urging athletes to "be vigilant" in using them.
And if you test positive for a prohibited substance, consuming it unintentionally can result in the same four-year ban as if you deliberately took it.
