articles.title: WWE's Growing Problem with Oba Femi
articles.summary: Oba Femi has had a breakout year for WWE, enjoying a magical run through the main roster that has seen him dominate the competition, defeat Brock Lesnar in two of their three wars and win the King of the Ring tournament.
articles.body:
Oba Femi has had a breakout year for WWE, enjoying a magical run through the main roster that has seen him dominate the competition, defeat Brock Lesnar in two of their three wars and win the King of the Ring tournament.

Femi is incredibly popular with fans and looks every bit the future star that Lesnar labeled him at the conclusion of their Hell in a Cell Match at SummerSlam.

However, The Ruler's meteoric rise and early career triumphs are not without a significant growing problem for WWE.

Femi exploded onto the scene in WWE and within three months of his main roster call-up, defeated Lesnar clean and in the center of the ring.

He lost the next matchup, but put an end to The Beast Incarnate's Hall of Fame-worthy career inside the unforgiving confines of Hell in a Cell at SummerSlam in their third encounter.

There is no better way for WWE to have introduced Femi to the fans and announced him as the next big thing than the way he has been booked.

However, when a star arrives in WWE and immediately conquers the seemingly unconquerable, there are only so many directions they can go and still maintain their momentum.

For Femi, beating and retiring Lesnar was a blessing and a curse in that the only logical next step for him is vanquishing Roman Reigns or CM Punk and claiming one of the company's top two titles.

WWE, however, appears content to deliver the slow build, with Femi likely winning the men's Royal Rumble match in January 2027 and challenging for one of those titles at WrestleMania 43.

The Show of Shows is still nearly nine months away.

The only thing that can possibly happen between now and then is that Femi loses momentum. Even his rivalry with Bron Breakker, a showdown between two men expected to carry WWE well into the future, feels like a step down for The Ruler.

That is not an indictment of Breakker. There are levels to this, though, and to suggest he has not been adversely affected by baffling creative would be an understatement.

A match with Femi clearly means more to Breakker than it does to The Ruler.

That there is unlikely to be a clean finish means the two will keep each other busy for a few months. That will benefit one half of the pairing while leaving fans to speculate when Femi will step up to Reigns.

WWE Creative has not had the best track record over the last two years, with head-scratching decisions hurting story progression, leading to nonsensical developments and stunting the growth of some of its top young stars.

Case in point, Breakker, who returned at WrestleMania 42, defeated Seth Rollins at Backlash, but ultimately lost that feud and has been saddled in a tag team with Austin Theory ever since.

It would be fair to question whether WWE can effectively push Femi in a way that does not undo everything it has accomplished with him to this point.

One loss here, or a bad segment of TV there, could do considerable damage and threaten it all. Lesnar put Femi in a prime position to go out and succeed as the new smashing badass in WWE.

If someone in the room overthinks a single match or moment, it could unravel, and Femi's aura and popularity will be adversely affected. Again, nine months is a long time, with plenty of opportunities for someone to make a call that sabotages the biggest slam dunk the company has had in decades.

Yes, WWE has carefully booked Femi to this point, except for the guaranteed title shot he willingly gave up to battle Lesnar at SummerSlam. But that was a momentary lapse with little ill-effect.

The company will not be that lucky if it fails him on the road to what feels like an inevitable and appropriate coronation as soon as WrestleMania next spring.

Holding off on crowning Femi champion at that event would only deepen WWE's growing problem.

articles.title: Former Olympian Jenny Simpson Says She Has to End Running Career After Cardiac Arrest in Race
articles.summary: Olympic medalist Jenny Simpson says she will not run again after suffering cardiac arrest while running a pacer mile at a June track event in Raleigh.
articles.body:
Olympic medalist Jenny Simpson says she will not run again after suffering cardiac arrest while running a pacer mile at a June track event in Raleigh.

Simpson shared the update in a Thursday post on her Instagram .

After being treated for heart failure, Simpson said she was diagnosed with an inherited heart condition known as "Arrhythmogenic Right Ventricular Cardiomyopathy."

"Scar tissue within my heart disrupted its electrical system, triggering dangerous heart rhythms that ultimately caused my heart to stop," Simpson wrote.

Simpson continued, "My future is an incredible gift. It's hopeful, and it has great purpose. But my diagnosis also means it would be dangerous for me to return to running.

"That chapter has ended. Thankfully, my story hasn't."

Simpson, 36, represented the United States in three Olympics. She won 1,500-meter gold at the 2011 World Championships and bronze in the same event at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

The Associated Press first reported Simpson had been treated with CPR and an automated external defibrillator (AED) after collapsing on the track at the Sir Walter Miler on June 16.

Simpson wrote in her post that care "kept me alive until EMS arrived."

"After arriving at the hospital, I went into cardiac arrest again," Simpson wrote. "My heart continued to fail, and I was placed on life support before being transferred to Duke Hospital for more advanced heart failure support."

"And then, miraculously, my heart woke back up. My whole body proved remarkably resilient. Within days my heart and lungs were strong enough to work on their own."

Simpson went on to express gratitude for her running career, which spanned from winning four NCAA titles with Colorado to becoming the first American woman to medal in the Olympic 1,500-meter.

"I couldn't have written a better ending. To have my final run be a one mile race on the track, pacing young girls and running in community... I'm in awe of the goodness of what God has given me," Simpson wrote.

Simpson says she plans to remain Colorado while working on her recovery plan with doctors at Duke. She added she will discuss her recovery further in a CBS Saturday Morning appearance scheduled for this weekend.

Simpson initially retired from competitive running in 2024 after completing the New York City Marathon. She was named Fleet Feet's first Chief Running Officer, a job which includes designing training programs for the retailer, in February.

articles.title: Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon Headline NHL 27's Player Ratings After Position-by-Position Reveal
articles.summary: Connor McDavid is in a league of his own, at least when it comes to NHL 27's new player ratings.
articles.body:
Connor McDavid is in a league of his own, at least when it comes to NHL 27's new player ratings.

The Edmonton Oilers star is the only player in the league to earn the coveted 99 overall rating in the latest edition of EA Sports' hockey game. He is followed closely behind by Nathan MacKinnon and Nikita Kucherov

Here is a look at the top players from each position, per the game's official website .

That McDavid is the top-ranked player comes as no surprise.

After all, the generational talent's resume features three Hart Memorial Trophies as the league MVP, five Ted Lindsay Awards as the league's Most Outstanding Player, six Art Ross Trophies as the league's top point scorer and a Conn Smythe Trophy as the Most Valuable Player of the playoffs.

He won that Conn Smythe Trophy during the 2024 playoffs when he led the Oilers to the Stanley Cup Final, although they lost in seven games to the Florida Panthers.

The future Hall of Famer appeared in all 82 games last season and led the league in points (138) and assists (90). He also finished with 48 goals, which was his highest mark since he led the league with 64 during the 2022-23 campaign.

In all, McDavid has led the NHL in points in six of his 11 seasons.

He has dominated the NHL throughout his career, and now gamers can dominate their opponents by controlling him as the only 99 overall player in the latest edition of NHL 27.

articles.title: FIFA Suspends 3 Argentina Players A Combined 18 Games For World Cup Final Scuffle
articles.summary: FIFA on Friday handed bans to three Argentina players, led by a 10-match suspension for midfielder Leandro Paredes, for striking Spain opponents moments after the World Cup final.
articles.body: FIFA banned three Argentina players on Friday, including a 10-match suspension for midfielder Leandro Paredes, for striking Spain opponents after losing the World Cup final. The ban for Paredes — who grabbed Spain's Eric Garcia by the throat and pushed Gavi to the ground — ranks with the FIFA sanctions for Uruguay forward Luis Suarez in 2014 as among the most severe in World Cup history. Argentina defender Nahuel Molina was handed a seven-game ban while Thiago Almada was given a one-game suspension. FIFA imposed fines of $90,000 on Paredes and Molina, and $30,000 for Almada. The ban for Paredes is effectively a one-year expulsion from the Argentina team as the FIFA calendar for national team schedules includes 10 games through June 2027. All of those games could be friendlies with no competitive games currently scheduled. Spain's Gavi also banned for game vs England Gavi also was banned for one game, which is a Nations League match for Spain against England at Wembley on Sept. 26. An Argentina coach, Roberto Ayala, also got a three-game ban and $30,000 fine. The Argentine Football Association was fined $110,000 for a range of incidents during the World Cup including players carrying a political banner about the Falkland Islands after the semifinal win against England, and discriminatory chants by fans. AFA also was ordered by FIFA to spend $100,000 on anti-racism projects. Argentina received $34 million in World Cup prize money from FIFA. Argentina expected to appeal AFA can appeal the longer sanctions and fines to FIFA, and likely after at the Court of Arbitration for Sport. "The AFA legal department will, in a timely manner, request from FIFA the grounds for the reviewable rulings in order to file appeals with the governing body’s appeal committee, while retaining the future option of appealing to the CAS as a final recourse," the federation said in a statement. Suárez and Simunic cases In 2014, Suárez was banned from all soccer for four months, including for his new club Barcelona, and eight more competition games for Uruguay for biting Italy defender Giorgio Chiellini in a World Cup group stage game in Brazil. Simunic used a megaphone to lead fans chanting a slogan used by the country's pro-Nazi regime during World War II. The on-field clashes at last month's final in East Rutherford, New Jersey — which were charged by FIFA as assault cases — came after Argentina lost a testy final to Spain where it was mostly outplayed and barely created a scoring chance. Spain forward Ferran Torres scored the only goal in the second period of extra time, after Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez was sent off. FIFA disciplinary judges also ordered Argentina to play its next home game in a stadium limited to 50% of capacity. FIFA deferred a second stadium sanction and a $100,000 for probationary periods. articles.title: Texans Sign 2 Veteran WRs Following Jayden Higgins' Season-Ending Injury
articles.summary: The Houston Texans brought in reinforcements at wide receiver after Jayden Higgins' season-ending injury.
articles.body: The Houston Texans reportedly signed wide receivers Sterling Shepard and Zay Jones on Friday.  The addition of both veterans comes on the day Houston placed second-year WR Jayden Higgins on season-ending injured reserve after tearing his ACL in Tuesday's practice.  Shepard and Jones will provide a boost to what was already a thin receiving corps even before the Higgins injury. Shepard is entering his 10th NFL season, and will be joining his third team. He spent the last two years with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the eight before that with the New York Giants.  Shepard peaked in his third NFL season when he hauled in 66 catches for 872 yards and four touchdowns.  Jones, on the other hand, is entering his ninth NFL season for his fifth team. He suited up for the Arizona Cardinals for the last two seasons. Jones also had his best season for the Texans' AFC South rival, the Jacksonville Jaguars, when he had 82 catches for 823 yards and five touchdowns in 2022. Shepard and Jones join Nico Collins, Tank Dell, Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson in the Texans' receiving room.  Higgins, though, was primed for a second-year breakout. After being selected with the second pick in the second round of the 2025 NFL Draft, Higgins had 525 yards and six touchdowns in his rookie season. He had received praise from Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley.  "He’s put in work. He’s so much more comfortable — I thought he was comfortable last year by season’s end. The familiarity with the details and nuances of the offense, he’s playing clean. He can play all over," Caley said last week. "He doesn’t have any limitations, he really doesn’t." Instead, it will be a lost season for Higgins. As he recovers, the Texans will try to make up for his loss with the help of Shepard and Jones.

articles.title: BS Meter on Sami Zayn Injury, John Cena Classic Plans and More WWE Rumors
articles.summary: The pro wrestling rumor mill isn't exactly taking a break in the post-SummerSlam haze.
articles.body:
The pro wrestling rumor mill isn't exactly taking a break in the post-SummerSlam haze.

Sure, WWE doesn't have landmark events like Money in the Bank and Survivor Series until October and November, respectively.

But with headline items like Solo Sikoa's ascension and the usual buzz about free agents, company-hopping and so much more going on, there's quite a bit of ground to cover in these supposedly quiet times.

To help fans keep pace with the wild rumor mill, let's place the must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss.

The Solo Sikoa rise is very real and very not-stopping. According to WRKD Wrestling (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), it's not just fans embracing him, with the backstage reaction to Solo's rise being very positive, too.

How can anyone not love this? Sikoa is 33 and starting to emerge by seeming to genuinely be more himself . And he's doing it at a time when WWE desperately needs new top stars for the long-term next to Oba Femi.

No reason to doubt this one. There's also no reason to think Sikoa won't keep climbing. He's super funny, an in-ring threat and just easy to cheer for, in a young-Rock sort of way.

SmackDown might be headed for another change here soon. According to WrestleVotes Radio (h/t Mrosko ), the current plan in WWE is for the blue brand to go back to the three-hour runtime early next January.

WWE ebbs and flows in a seasonal way these days with the runtime here. Ramping it back up after the new year to give storylines more breathing room and more wrestlers screentime as they head for WrestleMania makes some sense.

This making sense doesn't necessarily mean it's good for fans, since the runtime can be a drag. Still, SmackDown looks stacked with CM Punk, Cody Rhodes and so many other major names, so it's the premier brand right now and could make it work well enough.

Is Sami Zayn actually injured? According to PW Insider (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), Zayn wasn't exaggerating on SmackDown recently when he talked about dealing with a broken hand.

WWE fans last saw Zayn in a match with the likes of Kevin Owens in that Fatal 4-Way on Night 2 of SummerSlam at the start of August. This on-air reveal by Zayn, then, might really have some backing behind it.

This would be an odd thing to lie about on television and would help explain the in-ring absence. Silver lining? There's a bit of a lull in the schedule right now, so Zayn can get right, then perhaps be in the mix around landmark stuff like Money in the Bank soon.

Anyone remember the John Cena Classic? The supposed tournament (or whatever it is/will be) is apparently on the docket for some time after Survivor Series, according to PW Insider (h/t Knight ).

The John Cena Classic sort-of reveal got some wild backlash right away. The ill-explained, supposed upcoming event was apparently going to let fans vote on who advances through tournaments, despite the actual in-ring winner. Or something, anyway.

Hard to buy this one. It's also hard to think WWE has any real plans to do this thing, except for the fact that it was announced at all. John Cena himself has said as recently as a few months ago that they're still trying to figure it out. The rushed-feeling announcement of the event probably won't lead to anything meaningful until there's a spot in the schedule where it would actually make sense to use it for a storyline. So, maybe not in 2026 at all.

A return here almost happened? According to False Finish (h/t Knight ), Ilja Dragunov and WWE were close to a deal for a post-SummerSlam return before he decided he wasn't interested.

This might not be the last time in 2026 that fans hear about a wrestler on an expiring contract with little recent television time who elects to go somewhere else. With the company cutting major would-be-lifers like New Day, some of the depth names on the roster could choose to leave after seeing the writing on the wall.

Fair enough. WWE surely saw the value in keeping Dragunov, even if he was being used sparingly. And it's easy enough to believe he's one of the individuals not content to just sit in the back and not get out there in the ring when the red light is on.

According to WrestleVotes Radio (h/t Knight ), WWE has pulled back from plans to have a Lil Yachty concert at September's Sunday Night's Main Event in response to recent happenings.

Said recent happenings include the New York Knicks dominating a recent Saturday Night's Main Event this summer. One could also whisper about a guy named Pat McAfee and stuff at WrestleMania, but the SNME-Knicks stuff is a fresher, more understandable mention.

Here's to hoping WWE sees the writing on the wall with celebrities. Then again, Lil Yachty has had a really solid run alongside wrestlers in programs lately, so it's a little unfortunate for him. Even so, more spotlight on wrestlers at wrestling shows…would be nice.

articles.title: Did Montez Ford Diss Roman Reigns with 'The Rock' Punchline on New Album?
articles.summary: WWE Superstar Montez Ford seemingly took a shot at Roman Reigns in a track from his new album, which dropped this week.
articles.body:
WWE Superstar Montez Ford seemingly took a shot at Roman Reigns in a track from his new album, which dropped this week.

During the song "Iced Out" from the AfterTheTide album (h/t Felix Upton of Ringside News), Ford dropped a line where he said, "Next on my list… but The Rock said, 'What'd the dude say?' Head of the Table? You're more or less than a toupee."

The Head of the Table is one of Reigns' many monikers, referring to his standing within the Samoan wrestling dynasty.

Ford, who is one half of the Street Profits tag team with Angelo Dawkins, has had some run-ins with Reigns over the years.

Most notably, Ford faced Reigns in a singles match on a September 2021 episode of SmackDown. Reigns was victorious, but Ford impressed and showed the potential to be a singles star down the line.

That hasn't yet come to fruition, though, as Ford remains in a tag team with Dawkins. The Street Profits haven't been seen on WWE programming since early last month, though, perhaps because of Ford and fellow WWE Superstar and wife Bianca Belair celebrating the birth of their first child together.

As for Reigns, he is still atop the mountain in WWE just like he was in 2021, as he is the reigning world heavyweight champion and the face of Raw.

Reigns is currently occupied with LA Knight and Solo Sikoa, but running back Reigns vs. Ford at some point is something many wrestling fans would undoubtedly love to see.

articles.title: Super League: St Helens keep play-off hopes alive with victory against Castleford as Toulouse and Hull both win
articles.summary: St Helens keep their play-off hopes alive with victory over Castleford, despite finishing with 10 men; Hull KR slump to a second home Super League defeat of the week and Jake Arthur lands a late drop goal to seal a thrilling fightback for Hull
articles.body:
St Helens called on six different try-scorers to beat Castleford 36-12 and keep their play-off hopes alive, despite finishing the match at the Brewdog Stadium with only 10 men.

It has been a dramatic week for Castleford, whose former head coach Ryan Carr announced he was leaving the club for "personal reasons" on Friday.

Saints also announced a coaching change this week, with Kevin Walters due to join from next season.

  • Super League fixtures & results | Super League table
  • Get Sky Sports or stream contract-free on NOW
  • Choose the Sky Sports notifications you want

The Australian's new side took an early lead, and tries from Jack Welsby, Shane Wright, Jacob Douglas, Tom Humphreys and Tristan Sailor made it 30-0 before the break.

Captain Jackson Hastings had added five goals, but lost his cool and was sent off after an altercation with Tyler Dupree for violent conduct.

Dupree was sin-binned for the same incident, and tempers continued to flare as the teams disappeared down the tunnel for the break.

Nene McDonald added a sixth try for the hosts after the break, making a Castleford comeback look increasingly unlikely.

Louis Senior and Laulu-Togaga'e finally got them on the board, before Saints finished the game with 10 men after Alex Walmsley and Chris Matagi were both sent to the sin bin.

St Helens interim boss Eamon O'Carroll told BBC Radio Merseyside: "I said I wanted to see the attitude of the players, and what better way to display that than when you go down to 10 men for 45 minutes?

"The players were fantastic. We simplified a few things, which probably helped, because everyone knew what the role was and their position."

Commenting on Hastings' dismissal, Castleford director of rugby Chris Chester told Sky Sports: "Scott Murrell just jumped (in the way of Dupree). We all know the rules, you can't punch people in the face.

"We'll let the disciplinary (match review panel) deal with those kinds of things. That's what they're there for."

Hull KR slump to another home defeat

Hull KR slumped to a second home defeat of the week as Toulouse ran out deserved 32-12 winners following a ruthless second half at Craven Park.

The Robins were beaten at home by play-off rivals Warrington on Tuesday night, and head coach Willie Peters dropped both Tevita Pangai Junior and Mikey Lewis following their upcoming bans which were handed out in the wake of the 34-28 defeat against the Wolves.

It was a scrappy start - much to the frustration of the expectant Hull KR fans - as Toulouse dug in during the opening 20 minutes and then exerted some control before Mathieu Jussaume scored the opening try on the half-hour when he broke through down the right.

The defending champions, chasing a home play-off berth, finally sparked into life when substitute Elliot Minchella went over in the 35th minute after a surging run by Peta Hiku, with Rhyse Martin adding the extras to make it 6-6 heading into half-time.

Toulouse opted to kick for a penalty early in the second half after a late tackle from Tom Amone, but Cesar Rouge saw his 35-metre attempt bounce off the crossbar.

Hull KR continued to be pushed back and Toulouse deservedly did get themselves in front again after 57 minutes when Benjamin Laguerre burst down the left and fed Romeo Tropis to go on to touch down under the sticks.

Toulouse further extended their advantage when Anthony Marion got on the end of a kick through and barged over, with the try given following a lengthy video review which showed the ball had been grounded after Hull KR initially had looked to have held him up.

Hull KR, who face leaders Wigan next week, crumbled again when Paul Ulberg was played into space down the left corner after 65 minutes before Tropis burst clear through down the other channel. Luke Polselli added another late scrappy Toulouse try after a kick bounced off the post and Louix Gorman got a consolation score for the home side in the closing stages with a fast break down the left.

Arthur's late drop goal seals Hull fightback

Hull half-back Jake Arthur landed a late drop goal to seal his side's thrilling fightback as they beat Catalans Dragons 27-26 at the Gilbert Brutus Stadium.

Arthur coolly slotted over a match-winning one-pointer with six minutes left to clinch Hull victory over former boss John Cartwright's Catalans and just their second win in 10 Super League games.

Hull trailed 26-14 early in the second half, but came storming back through converted tries from Harvie Hill and Aidan Sezer to tie the scores before Arthur's match-winning effort.

The visitors led through early tries from Logan Moy and Lewis Martin and led 14-12 at half-time after Catalans had hit back through touchdowns from Charlie Staines and Kruise Leeming.

Catalans appeared to take control of the match when Edenn Rogers-Smith and Leo Darrelatour both went over early in the second period, either side of Guillermo Aispuro-Bichet's penalty, to put them 26-14 ahead.

But Hull launched their fightback as Hill and Sezer both went over for converted scores in the space of six minutes and Arthur had the final word.

Hull have climbed up one place to 11th in the table, while Catalans sit ninth after their 15th defeat of the season.

Hull interim head coach Andy Last said: "It was a nail-biting game, it went right down to the wire. I'm just really proud of the playing group.

"I spoke all week about showing our personality and our performance when it gets tough and to make sure you answer those questions with your effort and your actions."

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

St Helens called on six different try-scorers to beat Castleford 36-12 and keep their play-off hopes alive, despite finishing the match at the Brewdog Stadium with only 10 men.

It has been a dramatic week for Castleford, whose former head coach Ryan Carr announced he was leaving the club for "personal reasons" on Friday.

Saints also announced a coaching change this week, with Kevin Walters due to join from next season.

The Australian's new side took an early lead, and tries from Jack Welsby, Shane Wright, Jacob Douglas, Tom Humphreys and Tristan Sailor made it 30-0 before the break.

Captain Jackson Hastings had added five goals, but lost his cool and was sent off after an altercation with Tyler Dupree for violent conduct.

Dupree was sin-binned for the same incident, and tempers continued to flare as the teams disappeared down the tunnel for the break.

Nene McDonald added a sixth try for the hosts after the break, making a Castleford comeback look increasingly unlikely.

Louis Senior and Laulu-Togaga'e finally got them on the board, before Saints finished the game with 10 men after Alex Walmsley and Chris Matagi were both sent to the sin bin.

St Helens interim boss Eamon O'Carroll told BBC Radio Merseyside: "I said I wanted to see the attitude of the players, and what better way to display that than when you go down to 10 men for 45 minutes?

"The players were fantastic. We simplified a few things, which probably helped, because everyone knew what the role was and their position."

The Robins were beaten at home by play-off rivals Warrington on Tuesday night, and head coach Willie Peters dropped both Tevita Pangai Junior and Mikey Lewis following their upcoming bans which were handed out in the wake of the 34-28 defeat against the Wolves.

It was a scrappy start - much to the frustration of the expectant Hull KR fans - as Toulouse dug in during the opening 20 minutes and then exerted some control before Mathieu Jussaume scored the opening try on the half-hour when he broke through down the right.

The defending champions, chasing a home play-off berth, finally sparked into life when substitute Elliot Minchella went over in the 35th minute after a surging run by Peta Hiku, with Rhyse Martin adding the extras to make it 6-6 heading into half-time.

Toulouse opted to kick for a penalty early in the second half after a late tackle from Tom Amone, but Cesar Rouge saw his 35-metre attempt bounce off the crossbar.

Hull KR continued to be pushed back and Toulouse deservedly did get themselves in front again after 57 minutes when Benjamin Laguerre burst down the left and fed Romeo Tropis to go on to touch down under the sticks.

Toulouse further extended their advantage when Anthony Marion got on the end of a kick through and barged over, with the try given following a lengthy video review which showed the ball had been grounded after Hull KR initially had looked to have held him up.

Hull KR, who face leaders Wigan next week, crumbled again when Paul Ulberg was played into space down the left corner after 65 minutes before Tropis burst clear through down the other channel. Arthur coolly slotted over a match-winning one-pointer with six minutes left to clinch Hull victory over former boss John Cartwright's Catalans and just their second win in 10 Super League games.

Hull trailed 26-14 early in the second half, but came storming back through converted tries from Harvie Hill and Aidan Sezer to tie the scores before Arthur's match-winning effort.

The visitors led through early tries from Logan Moy and Lewis Martin and led 14-12 at half-time after Catalans had hit back through touchdowns from Charlie Staines and Kruise Leeming.

Catalans appeared to take control of the match when Edenn Rogers-Smith and Leo Darrelatour both went over early in the second period, either side of Guillermo Aispuro-Bichet's penalty, to put them 26-14 ahead.

But Hull launched their fightback as Hill and Sezer both went over for converted scores in the space of six minutes and Arthur had the final word.

Hull have climbed up one place to 11th in the table, while Catalans sit ninth after their 15th defeat of the season.

Hull interim head coach Andy Last said: "It was a nail-biting game, it went right down to the wire. I'm just really proud of the playing group.

articles.title: WWE Contracts, '90-Day No-Compete Clause' Finally Explained by Former Champion in New Video
articles.summary: WWE is rumored to be going through roster cuts sometime soon, and one wrestler who went through that experience shined some light on how things play out.
articles.body:
WWE is rumored to be going through roster cuts sometime soon, and one wrestler who went through that experience shined some light on how things play out.

Raj Dhesi, formerly known as one-time WWE Champion Jinder Mahal, resurfaced his video explaining why wrestlers are required to sit out for 90 days after being cut, even though "there is no such thing as a no-compete clause in WWE."

"When you sign a WWE contract, in the writing it states, 'WWE can terminate your contract with 90 days' notice.' So when you receive the phone call, it's them letting you know that in 90 days, your contract is cut," Dhesi explained. "They will pay you for the 90 days. That distinction is very important, because if it was a no-compete clause, you would not get paid for 90 days. For 90 days, you are still under WWE contract."

ESPN Addresses 'Completely False' Rumors About Future WWE Contract

Dhesi went on to add that wrestlers who are cut are pulled from live events and shows to protect both themselves and the company from future liabilities such as injuries or misrepresenting the brand in any way.

"In my opinion, WWE paying you for 90 days is an incredible gesture," Dhesi said. "It gives you time to reorganize your life. You're not making moves out of desperation or anger, and it actually protects both parties."

articles.title: Texans Reportedly Acquire WR Kayshon Boutte From Patriots For S Jaylen Reed
articles.summary: The Houston Texans reportedly acquired wide receiver Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots on Monday in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft pick.
articles.body: The Houston Texans are adding much-needed depth at wide receiver.  Houston has agreed to a deal to acquire wide receiver Kayshon Boutte from the New England Patriots in exchange for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft pick, The Ringer reported on Monday.  The draft selection sent to New England originally belonged to the New Orleans Saints, according to NFL Network. The trade addresses an immediate roster need for Houston following a season-ending knee injury to wide receiver Jayden Higgins during last week's joint practice session with the Las Vegas Raiders. Higgins was expected to hold a starting role in the Houston offense before suffering a torn ACL. Boutte spent his first three seasons with New England after being selected in the 2023 draft. Last season, the receiver recorded 33 receptions for 551 yards and six touchdowns in a bit of a breakout year. However, Boutte became expendable this offseason following the Patriots' moves at wide receiver. They made a big trade for A.J. Brown and signed Romeo Doubs to a pricey contract. Brown and Doubs joined a wide receiver room that also features DeMario "Pop" Douglas, Kyle Williams and Mack Hollins.  So, Boutte's name emerged in trade rumors over the offseason and into training camp. He addressed the trade speculation during training camp last week. "I'm just blocking out the noise. That's the main thing. We all hear the stuff that's going on," Boutte told reporters. "But like I always said, I'm where I'm at. My feet are here, so I'm not worried about what's next or what's behind me. Just being present." In return, New England acquires Reed to bolster their secondary along with future draft compensation. Boutte now joins a Houston receiving group that features Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel, and Tank Dell. articles.title: WWE Raw Live Updates, Results and Highlights From Aug. 24
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of WWE Raw on August 24. Scroll down for updates of all the action from Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's live coverage of WWE Raw on August 24. Scroll down for updates of all the action from Ottawa, Ontario, Canada.

OTM put Jimmy through the announce table while Keys held Jey and forced him to watch. The show ended with Knight, Solo and The Usos all down around the ring as OTM and Keys stood tall in the ring.

The Usos still had the upper hand all through the break into the next segment. They kept Sikoa isolated with quick tags and double-team moves.

The Street Champ hit a desperate clothesline to give himself some breathing room. Knight and Jimmy both tagged in at the same time. The Megastar unloaded on the elder Uso with jabs and a clothesline.

As Jey and Solo were fighting at ringside, Royce Keys put both of them through the barricade with a huge Spear. In the ring, OTM from NXT attacked Knight and Big Jim.

Bronco Nima and Lucien Price helped Keys destroy all four men. It looks like we officially have a new trio on Raw to compete with The Bloodline.

The Usos vs. LA Knight and Solo Sikoa Part 1

Jimmy and LA came out of the gate hot as soon as the bell rang. Knight hit a clothesline to get the first takedown before tagging in Solo for a double back elbow.

The Usos were able to take control with some combined attacks. They took Solo out of the ring and drilled him with a double superkick.

After a video hyping Zilla Fatu in NXT, Chad Gable was talking to Pearce backstage, and the GM said he is going to go find a new challenger for him. Ethan Page walked up and congratulated him on winning the IC title from Rey Mysterio.

All Ego said Gable is intimidated by him, but Gable reminded him that he beat him to earn the title shot in the first place. He said he would have given Page a title shot, but the way he is acting has made him change his mind.

Back in the arena, The Usos came out for their match against Sikoa and Knight.

Penta had control through the break, but the living skeleton started to regain his footing. He took Penta down with a few high-flying moves and scored a two-count with a powerslam.

La Parka drilled the former IC champion with a DDT for a close two-count. Penta caught him with a Penta Driver, but he couldn't keep him down for the pin.

A Spanish Fly got La Parka another near-fall before Penta wrenched his arm behind his back. He hit the Mexican Destroyer to seal the victory and advance to the finals.

This was a solid match, but the most intriguing part of this is that we will see Penta and Fenix fight in the finals next week to determine who gets to face Roman Reigns for the world title in Mexico City.

Lyra Valkyria had a brief exchange with Sol Ruca and Iyo Sky before Penta made his way out first to take on La Parka in the other semifinal match in the ongoing No. 1 Contender's tournament.

The luchadores started with a fast-paced exchange, but Penta took control. He sent La Parka out of the ring so he could take him down with a dive through the ropes.

La Parka recovered and hit a moonsault from the middle rope to the floor. Penta caught him with a superkick as he was coming off the top rope, but it only got him a two-count.

We returned to see Cass missing a corner splash. Evans tried to build a little momentum, but he couldn't take Cass off his feet. The big man caught him, but Evans sent him over the top rope before hitting a suicide dive.

The Young OG put Cass in the timekeeper's area so he could hit a running dive over the barricade. Evans started unloading on him with punches and kicks.

He brought Cass back in the ring and hit the Red Dot kick and a springboard clothesline. He went for the OG Cutter, but Cass shoved him off the top turnbuckle.

He nailed Je'Von with a big boot for the win. This seemed like a pretty abrupt ending, and an odd choice for a finishing move.

Judgment Day attacked Evans after Cass left the ring and left him down and out.

Big Cass has been making Evans' life hard recently, so they met in what was the first match Cass has had in WWE since returning. The way they shot the entrance for Cass was designed to make him look as big as possible, and it worked.

Evans tried to stick and move to avoid the big man. He brought the powerhouse out of the ring with a hurricanrana, but when he went for a slingshot crossbody, Cass caught him. Je'Von got back in the ring and Cass leveled him with a clothesline over the top rope.

Michael Cole talked about the journey Cass has been on since he was fired by WWE eight years ago as we saw him throw Evans into the barricade. He said Cass has taken no accountability for his actions.

Paul Heyman and Adam Pearce were in the ring for a contract signing between Oba Femi and Bron Breakker. The Ruler made his entrance first as the crowd chanted his name.

Breakker asked Femi who he thinks he is, claiming to be the future. He asked what Femi has done to earn the title of being the future of WWE. He diminished Femi's King of the Ring win and victory over Brock Lesnar.

He talked a lot of trash about how Femi wouldn't even be where he is if Breakker hadn't been out with an injury for months. The Ruler called him an angry, orange man and said he can't understand that his chances of being the face of WWE are gone.

Breakker signed the contract and said Femi is going to realize he is the one guy he can't beat. He taunted Oba by saying Heyman should sign it for him since they are so close now.

Bron and Oba ended up brawling after Breakker threatened Heyman. Austin Theory showed up to help his partner, but Femi fought them off and put Theory through the table.

We returned to see both men trading chops. Lee hit a few kicks to take Fenix off his feet. He hit a beautiful float over into a powerbomb, but it couldn't get him the win.

They continued to trade fast-paced offense until they ended up fighting near the announce table. Fenix was tripped on the table, which gave Lee an opening to hit a massive cannonball through the second rope that hit Fenix off the top of the table.

That spot was wild! The crowd chanted "This is awesome" as Lee brought Fenix in for a tornado DDT to get a two-count. Rey hit a brainbuster as he began regaining momentum.

He got Lee up for the Mexican Muscle Buster, but Lee countered into the Styles Clash for a near-fall. They kept going back and forth until Fenix finally hit his finisher to get the win.

This match was incredible. If you are not watching the show live, make sure you check this one out. Both guys worked their butts off to make this awesome.

The No. 1 Contender's tournament continued this week with Rey Fenix taking on Dragon Lee in the semifinals. Before the match, Je'Von Evans attacked Dom Mysterio and JD McDonagh backstage, which Rey Mysterio seemed to love.

They started with a quick exchange of holds and counters. Neither man could get an advantage as they went move for move. They came to a stalemate before they began trading strikes.

Lee was the first one to take control with a nice dropkick in the corner for a two-count, but Fenix wasn't down for long. He hit the running kick across the top rope he is known for, and he followed it with a diving crossbody for a near-fall.

The AAA cruiserweight champion hit a moonsault on the floor, but when they got back into the ring, Lee hit a German suplex. He took Fenix down with a huge dive over the top rope that sent us into the break.

Perez had control through the break, but Vaquer was starting to make a comeback when we returned. Roxy had to pull her hair to escape an abdominal stretch, but the former world champion maintained control.

She used the Devil's Kiss to slam Roxanne's head into the mat 10 times. She used a brutal dragon screw leg whip in the corner before hitting a running double knee against the turnbuckle.

Perez recovered and hit a nice shining wizard for a two-count. Stephanie countered a crossface into a package backbreaker. Morgan interfered while Rodriguez distracted the ref. This brought out Becky Lynch.

Roxy tried to take advantage of all the mayhem, but Vaquer was able to hit her with her finisher to score the win.

Lynch took Morgan out at ringside before getting into the ring. She and Vaquer exchanged a few words before The Man made her exit.

Stephanie Vaquer vs. Roxanne Perez Part 1

Stephanie Vaquer returned to action for the first time since WrestleMania to take on Roxanne Perez. La Primera made her way to the ring right before the break. Liv Morgan and Raquel Rodriguez were at ringside.

Perez played some mind games by avoiding Vaquer a few times before slapping her and then hiding in the ropes. Once Vaquer got her hands on her, she wrestled her to the mat and stomped on her elbow.

Roxy fooled her into chasing her back into the ring. They traded stiff slaps before Stephanie almost locked her in an armbar. Vaquer hit a running kick in the corner, but a distraction from Raquel allowed Perez to shove her off the top rope.

LA Knight came to the ring to kick things off with a promo. He said he needs to talk about the coward, Roman Reigns.

He talked about Reigns refusing to defend the belt against him and how he wasn't able to compete in the current tournament going on with AAA.

Solo Sikoa appeared in the crowd and used Knight's own catchphrase before thanking him for helping out last week with The Bloodline. A moment later, The Usos started making their way to the ring.

When Jey sent him a warning shot, Solo pretended like he was in The Matrix to avoid it. They ended up agreeing to a tag match with the four of them for later in the show.

Knight and Sikoa are so great together. They are always funny whenever they interact.

Monday Night Raw is officially on the air. This week's episode had an early start time due to a double taping alongside SmackDown.

Shots of various Superstars backstage were shown before we went to a video recapping what happened last week with The Bloodline.

articles.summary: Here's what we learned from this week's preseason games.
articles.body: Two weeks of preseason games are in the books, and we're starting to see the light at the end of the tunnel.  This past week's slate of preseason games, plus joint practices, brought us more glimpses of what we could expect to see in the regular season. But it brought some drama, too. Deshaun Watson was named the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback on Monday after making pointed remarks to the team's fans following his lackluster performance on Saturday. There's also an unusual storyline developing with players who might wind up playing college football in the next couple of weeks.  So, with only one more preseason week to go, here are our takeaways from the latest slate of preseason games.  1. Deshaun Watson Didn’t Deserve The Starting Job In Cleveland. He Got It Anyway. Ralph Vacchiano: Deshaun Watson showed everyone on Saturday why he shouldn’t be the Cleveland Browns' starting quarterback, with a terrible on-field performance and an even worse one off the field. Then, Todd Monken gave him the job anyway.  Maybe that’s a sign that the new Browns coach had nothing but bad options in his quarterback competition, but his choice still couldn’t have been any worse. He went with a 30-year-old who’ll surely be an ex-Brown next season over a somewhat promising young quarterback, Shedeur Sanders. And he did it two days after Watson was terrible in a preseason game against the Bills (5 of 12 for 36 yards and an interception) and then showed an incredible lack of self-awareness (and an abundance of immaturity) when he whined about being booed. "I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do with the performance," Watson said. "It’s a little more personal than that. So, I think that’s a disrespectful thing." OK, that’s a little rich and a lot outrageous, coming from the man who got the biggest fully-guaranteed contract in NFL history from the Browns in 2022 (five years, $230 million) even though he hadn’t played in two years and was accused of sexual misconduct by 27 women. He then rewarded that startling generosity by only being healthy enough to play in 19 games over the last four seasons — and not particularly well, either. Even without that bad moment, though, Monken still made the wrong choice. The coach had been leaning this way, multiple team sources told me, in part because the Browns’ early schedule is overloaded with road games (their first two and six of their first nine), and Monken thought Watson’s veteran presence would help his young team. But Watson’s play didn’t warrant that faith. He was just 16 of 27 for 162 yards and an interception in two preseason games. His passer rating of 61.0 was even a notch below Sanders’ 65.2. So while it’s true that there was no good option here, it’s also true that really is no upside to Watson, who is understandably reviled by what seems to be a majority of the Browns’ fan base. Starting Sanders at least would’ve given them hope that he can get better, something to look forward to other than the QB-rich 2027 draft. Instead, Monken latched on to the anchor that has been scraping the Browns along rock bottom for the last five years. Sanders will surely get a shot later this season. But as usual in Cleveland, any hope for the future is delayed. 2. Yes, The Pipeline To The Pros Goes Both Ways Greg Auman: The most backwards trend of the NFL preseason? Marginal players testing the waters of playing in NFL preseason games and  … going back to college. It seems impossible, but these days, if you can get a judge to rule the right way, traditional lines of amateurism and eligibility can disappear. The NCAA’s shift to a five-year eligibility model wasn’t intended to be backdated for athletes who had exhausted their window – and signed a pro contract, gotten paid and even played for NFL teams. But that’s really happening, leaving general managers to wonder if they’ll lose players off their roster to the allure of NIL money from colleges. Tight end Dae’Quan Wright, an undrafted rookie with the Browns, put his name in the transfer portal. Cleveland has since waived him, setting him up to play for LSU this fall. "Man, ain’t this s--- crazy?" Browns coach Todd Monken said. "I mean, I don’t even know what to say … I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out a week ago. Now I know. I didn’t call him back, guess I should have." Speaking of LSU, consider Tampa Bay Buccaneers undrafted rookie linebacker Jack Pyburn, who had two sacks in Tampa Bay’s preseason opener. He’s also one of the players granted a temporary restraining order that could allow him to return to college football. He played at LSU last year, and that sets up the man-bites-dog possibility of an NFL player leaving early for college. The fall semester at LSU started on Monday, and NFL rosters will be cut from 90 players to 53 by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday. It’s unlikely the Bucs will keep Pyburn for their 53, but he has (had?) a good shot at their practice squad. That pays $247,500 for a full season, and Pyburn could make three or four times that much on the Van Wilder go-back-to-college route. Pyburn said after Saturday’s preseason game that his agents had told the Bucs that college was a potential "backup plan," but when pressed as to what he might decide if choosing between an NFL practice squad and going back to college, he was noncommittal. "Ultimately, that’s a decision I’m going to have to make with my family, talk to my agents and see what’s the best business decision and what’s the best option for me and my future career," he said. Yes, it’s NFL "respect my decision" season. Players would have to repay their NFL employers to regain college eligibility. Pyburn got a $15,000 bonus and $100,000 in guaranteed salary, but it’s possible that college NIL payments could also be covered by "offset" language standard in such contracts, normally intended so if NFL Team B pays a player to be on their practice squad, that subtracts from the money NFL Team A was on the hook for by their guarantee. The league will have to sort out the ramifications. Can a player already passed over once in the draft get another shot, like baseball players do? This was already happening with basketball and G League players showing up on college rosters, but for NFL teams, it’s made roster-building even more complicated by the idea that players can make more money playing football at a lower level. 3. Stetson Bennett Commands Offense, Cements Role As Rams' Backup QB Eric D. Williams: With Jimmy Garoppolo no longer on the roster, Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay’s search for someone to fill that void, should reigning MVP Matthew Stafford suffer an injury during the regular season, appears to be over. In the battle between Ty Simpson and Stetson Bennett, the Alabama product cracked the door open with a sparkling performance in a Week 1 preseason win over the Kansas City Chiefs. But Bennett may have closed the door by playing well in a 34-0 victory over the New Orleans Saints at SoFi Stadium. The Georgia product finished with two rushing touchdowns in the first half, leading the Rams to scoring drives on four of his five possessions. Bennett finished 19 of 31 for 181 yards, with no touchdown passes and no interceptions for a 77.5 passer rating.  Ty Simpson also played solidly, finishing 8 of 12 for 73 yards in the second half. Simpson led the offense on one scoring drive. However, Bennett impressed McVay by the way he led the offense, with quarterbacks coach and associated offensive coordinator Dave Ragone calling the plays – although he didn’t like Bennett reaching for the pylon with the ball on his first rushing touchdown. "I loved the fact that he used his legs," McVay said. "We’ll learn from reaching the ball into the end zone, even though I challenged that and we were successful. We don’t want to leave ourselves susceptible to losing the ball out of the end zone where it goes for a touchback. "But he did a great job. I thought he got an opportunity to really showcase a lot of his skills." 4. Daniel Jones Primed To Pick Up From Where He Left Off Last Season Ben Arthur: Watching the Indianapolis Colts quarterback at Wednesday’s joint practice with the Atlanta Falcons, it was impossible for me to tell that he tore his Achilles just eight months ago. Everything you want your passer to do — drop back, scramble, throw on the move, evade pressure — Jones looked normal in doing so. Oh, and he was carving up the Falcons’ secondary as well. With Indianapolis’ rushing attack struggling, Jones was near perfect in the pass game, targeting various receivers.  We still need to see Jones move and perform in games. But all the early signs suggest that he can pick up from last season, when he was playing the best ball of his career before a broken leg slowed him down and the Achilles injury ended his season.  "I think with any major rehab process, you're always kind of progressing and getting back and getting used to doing everything, building up the reps on it, building up just your conditioning level," Jones said Wednesday. "I feel really good and there's nothing I don't feel good doing." The Colts’ pass-catching situation around Jones is a bit shaky at the moment, given star tight end Tyler Warren (groin) and wide receiver Alec Pierce (offseason ankle surgery) are currently sidelined. But when they return, they’ll add to a group that features one of the league’s best slot receivers in Josh Downs and recent signee Keenan Allen, who’s been a dominant force on third down.  That’s a cast of receivers Jones can find success with.  "I think it could be really special, to be honest," Colts coach Shane Steichen said of the pass-catching group. "Alec (Pierce) obviously is a hell of a football player, which you guys know. [Josh] Downs, Tyler [Warren], and then adding Keenan [Allen] to the fold. I think we can do a lot with those guys and move bodies around and find matchups."  5. Let’s Have A Conversation About Chiefs Breakout Rookie WR Cyrus Allen Henry McKenna: If you’ve been following training camp for Kansas City, you’ve heard of Allen. If you’re the type who combs X for potential breakout stars in fantasy football, you’ve heard of Allen. If you’re obsessed with NFL rookies and the draft, you’ve heard of Allen.  His training camp highlights have been crazy. And Andy Reid didn’t slow the hype’s momentum. "He's done a nice job," Reid said of Allen. "The quarterback trusts him." This was the first week of training camp. Allen was a sixth-round pick out of Louisiana Tech. It felt like a big proclamation, particularly given that Rashee Rice has a history of missing time due to injuries and suspensions and Xavier Worthy has failed to live up to his first-round hype.  Since then, Allen has played well — steadily doing what he could to move up the depth chart. That included scoring touchdowns with the first-team when paired with Patrick Mahomes. That also included beating first-round cornerback Mansoor Delane in 1-on-1s and team drills (7x7 and 11x11), per reporters on the scene. But here’s the truth for anyone expecting the second coming of Tyreek Hill. The folks at Arrowhead Pride broke it down with depth. But it’s likely — perhaps even overly optimistic — to project 60 for Allen. And only six receivers converted 60 targets into 500+ receiving yards in 2025. But before he wows in the box score, he’ll need to land in the WR3 spot. Given that he was playing behind Tyquan Thornton and Jaylen Royals in the second preseason game, Allen appears to be WR5. For what it’s worth, Hill had 83 targets, 61 catches, 593 yards and six touchdowns in his rookie season. That would be a great year for Allen. So keep an eye on him. He’s a real playmaker. But let’s stay reasonable for a rookie in a Chiefs' offense that has a lot of mouths to feed. 6. De’Zhaun Stribling Shows Kyle Shanahan Knows How To Evaluate WRs Williams: NFL draft analysts were up in arms over the San Francisco 49ers taking Ole Miss product De’Zhaun Stribling in the second round, believing the organization had reached for a player that some consensus draft boards had going later in the draft. However, through two weeks of preseason play, Stribling has acquitted himself nicely. Stribling is tied for the league lead with 11 catches for 109 yards, with a long of 32 yards. He finished with four catches for 46 yards in a win over the Los Angeles Chargers this week.  I had a chance to watch Stribling in a joint practice at the Chargers’ facility. At 6-2 and 210 pounds, Stribling is an easy mover with suction-cup hands that can make contested catches in congested areas. Along with that, Stribling has the potential for explosive playmaking ability to do something after the catch, a key attribute in Shanahan’s offense. With Ricky Pearsall out for the year and Brandon Ayiuk no longer on the roster, Stribling should find a significant role in San Francisco’s offense this season. "I love how he handles himself," Shanahan said about Stribling. "He takes coaching well and never seems to take anything personally. He’s been a real fun guy to coach so far." 7. Bills’ Thin WR Corps May Be More Of A Problem Than Ever Vacchiano: One great NFL mystery of this generation will surely be why the Buffalo Bills, with arguably the best quarterback in the league in Josh Allen, keep failing to surround him with top-end receivers. And once again, heading towards a season they hope will end in a Super Bowl, that failure is being exposed. Though they are getting a solid performance this summer from D.J. Moore, the veteran "No. 1" wideout they acquired from the Chicago Bears, the rest of the corps is falling apart. Keon Coleman, their second-best receiver last season (38 receptions for 404 yards and four touchdowns), is nursing a concerning sprained toe. Khalil Shakir, last season’s top wideout (72 receptions for 719 yards and four touchdowns), missed the joint practices and preseason game against the Browns last week with an undisclosed injury. And rookie Skyler Bell, their fourth-round pick, has missed two weeks with a groin injury. That leaves Allen right now with Moore, who cost the Bills a second-round pick in March, Joshua Palmer (22 receptions for 303 yards and zero touchdowns) last season, and … not much else. That, of course, is not how the Bills see it. One team source told me their belief is that Allen can win with almost anyone around him, and that he can take what looks like a below-average group and make them much better. They are also convinced that Moore, at age 29, can reverse his steep, two-year decline simply by playing with an elite quarterback. It’s a gamble, of course, because otherwise all the pieces are in place in Buffalo: A powerful running game led by James Cook, a top offensive line, a top-10 defense that gets a boost from the addition of edge rusher Bradley Chubb. And of course, the brilliance of Allen will always give them a shot. Still, it’s hard not to imagine what this team would look like with just one elite receiver by Allen’s side. It would make their path to Buffalo’s first Super Bowl in 33 years look a lot easier than it currently is.

That leaves Allen right now with Moore, who cost the Bills a second-round pick in March, Joshua Palmer (22 receptions for 303 yards and zero touchdowns) last season, and … not much else. It’s a gamble, of course, because otherwise all the pieces are in place in Buffalo: A powerful running game led by James Cook, a top offensive line, a top-10 defense that gets a boost from the addition of edge rusher Bradley Chubb. articles.title: Why 49ers Appear To Be Driving Off The Cliff Entering 2026 Season
articles.summary: During Monday's edition of The Herd, Colin Cowherd evaluated the overall state of the 49ers, questioning whether San Francisco can maintain their position among the elite teams in the NFC.
articles.body: The San Francisco 49ers enter the upcoming regular season with expectations to remain competitive within arguably the best division in football while battling early injuries, older franchise mainstays returning from surgeries, and, most recently, off-field news involving the team's owner.  That doesn't seem to be a recipe for success, and Colin Cowherd agrees. During Monday's edition of The Herd, Cowherd questioned whether San Francisco can maintain its position among the elite teams in the conference. "I tend to think the Niners are very close to pulling a Thelma and Louise and driving off the cliff here," Cowherd said, comparing the 49ers to the hit '90s movie. On paper, the 49ers have reloaded with talent. They signed star wide receiver Mike Evans to beef up their wide receiver room and brought back Dre Greenlaw to solidify what they have at linebacker.  However, tight end George Kittle continues working back from Achilles surgery with a chance to play in Week 1, and running back Christian McCaffrey remains on a planned load management schedule during practice reps.  With that in mind, Cowherd pointed out that age and recovery timelines across essential positions present distinct hurdles for San Francisco when compared to younger rosters across the league. The roster remains heavily reliant on a core group of established veterans, several of which are returning from surgical procedures. "This is an old, old team, oldest roster in the NFL, and almost all their old guys are coming off serious surgeries," Cowherd said. "They are really dependent on five older players: Trent Williams, left tackle, he's 38. Kittle, going to be a hall of farmer, coming off surgery. Nick Bosa, coming off his second surgery. Christian McCaffrey led the NFL in touches. Mike Evans, who is often banged up, though I love him and Fred Warner off a surgery as well." San Francisco's depth issues have been compounded by injuries to recent high draft selections. "Don't forget their last two first-round picks: Ricky Pearsall, out for the year, injured. … Mykel Williams, who is a great young talent, he's banged up and won't be there for Week 1," Cowherd added. "They are hanging on by peptides and a prayer." Compared to the recent success NFC West rivals the Seahawks and Rams have had in the draft, the Niners will have their work cut out for them. "The Seahawks and the Rams have drafted so brilliantly over the last three years, very few misses. … Those are four games the Niners go in as an underdog," Cowherd said. San Francisco receives early scheduling relief to begin the regular season. Following their trip to Australia, the team returns home for consecutive games against the Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals before entering a more challenging stretch that includes matchups against the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos. Despite the favorable early home slate, Cowherd expressed skepticism regarding San Francisco's postseason prospects over a full 17-game schedule. "I don't think they're a playoff team," Cowherd said. "I love the coach. I love McCaffrey. I love the organization. I think they're heading right for a cliff." articles.title: Ex-Oregon State RB Anthony Hankerson Set For College Return After Being Waived By Seahawks
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks have waived running back Anthony Hankerson, who could try to play in college again.
articles.body: The Seattle Seahawks have waived running back Anthony Hankerson, who could try to play in college again. Hankerson signed with the Seahawks last week and rushed for 10 yards on five carries in their 19-16 preseason loss at Tennessee on Sunday night. He also caught two passes for nine yards. He is among 16 players who graduated high school in 2022 and became eligible to play a fifth collegiate season thanks to a Louisiana court order last week. Once he clears waivers, he could enter the transfer portal. Running back T.J. Harden, who played for the Seahawks in their preseason game against Dallas, was also among those granted a temporary restraining order by the Louisiana judge. Harden, who played last year at SMU and went undrafted, was waived by the Seahawks and entered the portal last week. Hankerson was an undrafted rookie out of Oregon State who signed with Miami in April, then was waived earlier this month. He ran for 1,086 yards and nine touchdowns last season, his second in Corvallis. He also had 22 catches for 123 yards. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Cal Raleigh Hits Career-High 3 Homers For Mariners Amid Season-Long Slump
articles.summary: Cal Raleigh busted out of a season-long slump with the first three-homer game of his career.
articles.body: Cal Raleigh busted out of a season-long slump with the first three-homer game of his career Monday night. The switch-hitting catcher capped a five-run first inning with a two-run shot off struggling Philadelphia Phillies ace Zack Wheeler. Raleigh added a leadoff homer against Wheeler in the fifth and a solo drive off reliever Chase Shugart in the seventh to give him 17 home runs this season. It was the first multihomer game of the year for Raleigh, who finished 3 for 3 with a walk in a 9-2 victory and raised his batting average from .159 to .167. Raleigh was runner-up for the AL MVP award last year, when he led the majors with 60 home runs and added 125 RBIs. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Sir Billy Boston: 'A world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told'
articles.summary: Rugby league commentator Matt Newsum says Sir Billy Boston was a "world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told".
articles.body:
When Sir Billy Boston was knighted in 2025, it was a unique moment for rugby league.

For the first time, this rebel sport from the north of England had been recognised in such a manner; one of its heroes had been acknowledged for their contribution to history through the game.

Sir Billy was a fitting recipient of the honour and a world-class athlete, whose story deserved to be told.

You can tell the importance of someone by how many statues have been erected in tribute, and Sir Billy Boston wasn't lacking.

His name was chosen as one of just five to grace Wembley's monument to rugby league's Challenge Cup, while years after his departure north, his home city of Cardiff also ensured his legacy remained cast-iron strong as he formed part of a three-man tribute along with Clive Sullivan and Gus Risman.

Unsurprisingly, Boston is also captured in bronze in his adopted home of Wigan; the place where his legend really came to life.

Born and brought up in Cardiff's ethnically-eclectic Tiger Bay district, he learned his rugby skills on the streets and with the talent factory-esque Cardiff International Athletic Club.

Like all Welsh lads he harboured dreams of playing for his local club Cardiff RFC and hopefully the national team.

Like others before and after for a time, Boston found those routes blocked, having to travel to Neath and Pontypridd to trial before his military service took him north.

It was here where the league scouts came calling, and Wigan persuaded Boston to turn professional in 1953, forever ending his union dreams in the time of 'sine die' penalties for liaising with league personnel.

Â£3,000 could easily buy a house at that stage, while it proved money well spent as he took to the new code like a duck to water, scoring with his first touch in a Wigan A team game.

This prime specimen of Welsh breezeblock had everything; he was quick, he could step and as former player and BBC commentator Ray French put it - his fend was like "being hit in the face with shovel".

The sepia footage and slow shutter speeds of the cameras that captured his magic during his playing days simply cannot dull his brilliance.

Whether it was bustling over for another try in cherry and white hoops at Wembley or crushing the Aussies at Sydney Cricket Ground, Boston was a blur of speed, footwork and power.

Having swiftly progressed to the first team at Central Park, he would go on to score 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan, and tales of his feats would be passed down through generations. There are very few down at the Brick Community Stadium these days who don't know of Sir Billy, young or old, his name carried a cache right until his last.

Great Britain gave him the international recognition denied to him by Wales, and he rewarded the selectors by racking up the tries, particularly against the Australians who would bear the brunt of his scoring ability.

He scored 36 tries alone on his maiden Great Britain tour, dazzling both Australia and New Zealand in 1954 under captain and fellow Welshman Dickie Williams.

Boston was a phenomenal rugby league player, but there is also a powerful message in how in post-war Britain a black athlete could become a hugely popular figure by communities adjusting to a new, more diverse world.

Others like Roy Francis beforehand, Johnny Freeman, and Colin Dixon, also became established names, but never quite sprinkled the same stardust as Sir Billy.

It paved the way for players such as Ellery Hanley and Martin Offiah to charm the public with their talents, while modern day talent such as Junior Nsemba and Kai Pearce-Paul continues to stand out in a sport which has broken down barriers for years.

Sir Billy had a unique unifying effect on a normally partisan and tribal rugby league community.

He was revered naturally in Wigan, his adopted home, but you won't hear a boo or jeer at mention of Boston anywhere - not even at sworn rivals St Helens where they appreciate a good footballer when they see one.

Still a regular visitor to Wigan games right up to his passing, it was always a beautiful moment when the cameras found him, the crowd spotting him on the screen bursting into cheer, and the realisation creeping over his face in the shape of a smile.

There was a photo of him and his wife Lady Joan, who had died just a few weeks previously, on her seat with flowers at Wigan's game with Wakefield last week. There is a poignancy that Sir Billy departed soon after her.

His seat will always be reserved at Wigan, and he will be dearly missed but certainly not forgotten.

The UFC welterweight champion believes Evloevâs youth could help him beat Volkanovski at UFC 333. Makhachev also feels the Australian is no longer at the same peak he reached a few years ago, even though he still sees him as one of the best fighters in the sport.Islam Makhachev predicts Movsar Evloev can beat Alexander VolkanovskiVolkanovski and Evloev will meet for the UFC featherweight title on October 24 at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi. The UFC has officially confirmed the fight as the main event of UFC 333. Volkanovski enters the bout as champion, while Evloev is still unbeaten with a 20-0 record.Makhachev knows what Volkanovski brings because the two have already fought twice. Their first meeting came at UFC 284, where Makhachev won a close decision. He then stopped Volkanovski with a head kick in the first round of their rematch at UFC 294.Now, despite those wins, Makhachev is not picking his former opponent to keep the featherweight belt.Speaking to reporters in Russia, Makhachev backed Evloev and pointed to the age gap between the two fighters.âItâs no secret and he himself knows that the fight wonât be easy, that Volkanovski is a tough opponent for anyone. But I think Movsar will manage with his youth. Volkanovski, honestly speaking, is not at the same peak he was a couple of years ago. Even though he is still one of the best fighters. I think itâll be a very competitive fight but I hope Movsar will do his job.âSherdog reported Makhachevâs prediction on August 25.The prediction is interesting because Makhachev did not dismiss Volkanovski. Instead, he pointed to something that could matter over five rounds: whether the 37-year-old champion can still perform at the level he showed during his best years.Evloev, meanwhile, has built an unbeaten record and earned his first UFC title shot. The UFCâs official event listing identifies him as the No. 1-ranked contender going into the fight.Alexander Volkanovski reveals what could happen after Movsar Evloev fightThere is another reason this title fight has extra weight for Volkanovski. The champion recently admitted that a very bad performance against Evloev could make him think about retirement.Volkanovski told 10 News that he has no plans to retire right now. However, he said the result and the damage from the fight could affect what he decides next.âIf things go terribly wrong, alright, weâre done. If things go very well, like the last one, no damage, go through, alright, weâll keep it rolling. Taking each fight as it goes, just trying to be real with it. But I donât have plans on retiring right now. Moneyâs always good.â MMA Fighting reported his comments.That puts more focus on what happens when Volkanovski faces the undefeated Evloev. Makhachev expects the younger challenger to take advantage, while Volkanovski is preparing to show that he still has enough to stay on top.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luke Littler's Players Championships finals dented by Jermaine Wattimena defeat
articles.summary: Luke Littler loses to Jermaine Wattimena in the quarter-finals of the 27th Players Championship contest of the year.
articles.body:
Luke Littler's hopes of qualifying for the Players Championship finals in November took a hit as he was defeated by Jermaine Wattimena in the quarter-finals of PC27 in Leicester.

Littler, playing in his first Pro Tour event in 2026, was forced into a last-leg decider, and the Dutchman hit a 115 checkout to claim his first victory in six meetings against Littler on the PDC tour.

The 19-year-old was in a positive mood afterwards though, posting "on the move" on Instagram.

Qualification for November's finals is important for Littler as he aims to complete the calendar sweep of ranking events in 2026.

The top 64 players in the Players Championship qualify for Minehead in November and Littler, who skipped the first 26 events on the circuit, sits in 141st place after claiming Â£4,000 on Tuesday.

There are seven Players Championship events remaining for The Nuke to get in to the top 64 - including one on Wednesday at the same venue.

However, he has previously stated his intention to only feature in the UK events, meaning he would only have three more opportunities to climb up the order of merit.

Littler is currently Â£22,250 behind 64th-placed Mario Vandenbogaerde. Victory at one of the events earns you Â£15,000, while runners-up receive Â£10,000.
